4070005e4307a161: KOTA BARU: "Based on the briefing given to the family yesterday, my child's body is intact, but we have to understand that a fire was involved," said Kamaruddin Salleh, 69.
Kamaruddin is the father of Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, who died in the helicopter crash near Long Lellang Airport, Ulu Baram, yesterday.

He said his daughter's body was expected to be brought back to Kelantan tomorrow and taken directly to Masjid Al-Karamah for funeral prayers before being buried at the Kampung Sri Kedeper Muslim cemetery.
"This is what we expect. The body will be brought back tomorrow once forensic procedures are completed.
"Yesterday, we were informed by the authorities that our child's body, along with the others, had been found, and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) samples had also been taken.
"Police also asked us not to view the body until the process is complete.
"We may be called to Miri Hospital today," he said when contacted today.
At the same time, the retired teacher expressed gratitude that his daughter's body, along with the others, had been found.
"Yesterday I was anxious when the initial information said only four had been found. Alhamdulillah, after that we were informed that all the victims had been found.
"I am grateful, because previously, we thought of all sorts of things given that they had fallen from a great height.
"Alhamdulillah, the entire operation yesterday went smoothly," he said.

Yesterday, media reported that the identities of all five victims killed in the helicopter crash and fire had been confirmed by the authorities through the identification of personal belongings found on their bodies.
The victims killed in the crash were Layang-Layang Aerospace pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, and Health Ministry medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33.
Also killed were community nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44, while another victim was assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31.
57f68e1f6f1ac023: LETTER: The deaths of five people in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash at Long Lellang, Sarawak, on Sept 8 should be a watershed moment for Malaysia's approach to airborne medical services.
They died while carrying out a service intended to bring healthcare to communities which are among the hardest to reach in the country. The investigation into the crash is ongoing.
However, we do not need to wait for that investigation to recognise that the system these healthcare workers operated in needs urgent, fundamental reform.

Malaysia's Flying Doctor Service began in Sarawak in 1973. More than half a century later, its purpose remains as important as ever. At least 97 locations in the Sarawak interior currently require and depend on the service.
What should concern us is that while medicine, aviation, and emergency care have transformed dramatically, how we organise and think about airborne healthcare still seems rooted in the 1980s.
Reports following the crash have highlighted several serious concerns. Personnel have undertaken missions without dedicated aviation safety training or clear aviation-specific insurance coverage.

The incentive for those undertaking FDS duty is RM30 for a return flight, unchanged since 1978. Shockingly, healthcare personnel on these medical missions are required to sign indemnity or liability-release forms before flying. Whoever required this of our healthcare professionals should be ashamed.
Who does a waiver protect?
The use of liability waivers for healthcare workers required to fly as part of their official duties must end. A waiver is not a safety policy

A doctor, nurse or medical assistant boarding an aircraft to serve patients in rural Sarawak is not going skydiving or participating in a recreational activity. They are performing public service on behalf of the government.

Ethically and from an occupational safety perspective, the principle should be straightforward. The organisations responsible for providing that service must manage the risks associated with an essential public service, not transfer them onto individual healthcare workers.
If we require people to fly for their jobs, then the system must protect them. It should not abandon them and their families in times of calamity.

Every member of an aeromedical team should have comprehensive aviation and occupational risk insurance covering accidental death, permanent disability, medical treatment, loss of income and appropriate compensation for dependants.
Operators must have adequate passenger and third-party liability insurance. Families should not have to rely on discretionary ex gratia payments after a tragedy.

Accountability is necessary. No waiver or insurance policy should protect an operator, contractor or government agency from responsibility if negligence, inadequate maintenance, deficient training or failure to meet required safety standards is eventually established.
Emphasising aeromedical service
Malaysia should stop thinking of the Flying Doctor Service primarily as a programme which sends Ministry of Health personnel into helicopters hired from contractors.
Modern aeromedical medicine is a specialised health service. An air ambulance is effectively an emergency department or intensive care transport platform in the sky.
The surrounding service must integrate aviation operations, clinical governance, medical equipment, communications, maintenance, training, and emergency preparedness. It is not a taxi.
A modern aeromedical service requires specialist pilots, flight nurses, retrieval physicians and paramedics who train and work together.

Healthcare personnel should receive mandatory aviation familiarisation and recurrent training covering emergency evacuation, rotor and propeller hazards, fire, hard landings, crash procedures, patient loading, and in-flight medical emergencies. These are not optional or nice-to-have.
Learn from the United Kingdom and Australia
The Health Ministry cannot be expected to go at this alone. The private sector must step up. United Kingdom offers a particularly interesting model for public-private partnership.

Twenty-one independent air ambulance charities operate across the UK. Collectively, they undertake more than 48,000 missions annually, almost entirely supported through public-private partnerships, operating alongside hospitals and ambulance services.

Australia provides another useful example. The Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS) is a charitable, not-for-profit health organisation delivering 24-hour emergency aeromedical retrieval and healthcare across vast rural and remote areas.
In 2023-24 alone, its aeromedical teams transported almost 33,000 Australians. The RFDS is neither completely government-run nor left entirely to charity.
The Australian government has a long-term strategic funding partnership. State governments, businesses, corporate partners, donors and communities also contribute. This model has been shown to work.
Malaysia needs a new model
We should consider establishing a Malaysian Aeromedical Service as a professional service through a public-private approach.

Its mission should be broader than the existing FDS. It should provide emergency medical evacuation, critical-care retrieval, inter-hospital transfers, medical repatriation, disaster response and scheduled outreach services throughout Malaysia.

The greatest need will naturally remain in Sabah and Sarawak, but such capability also has relevance to Orang Asli communities and remote areas of Peninsular Malaysia, offshore islands, maritime emergencies and major disasters.

The federal government would provide an assured baseline payment for essential services, based on coverage, readiness and agreed performance standards. Sabah and Sarawak governments could co-finance expanded regional capability.

Banks, telecommunications providers, energy companies, plantation businesses, mining and infrastructure companies (especially those whose operations depend upon rural and remote Malaysia) and even supermarket chains should become long-term corporate partners.
UK's Tesco heavily supports local and regional air ambulance services through partnerships and grants.

The Australian RFDS specifically identifies corporate partnerships, sponsorships, workplace giving, donations and even funding individual aircraft or specialised equipment as part of the ecosystem which sustains its work.

We have some of Southeast Asia's largest private hospital groups. We have major insurers, banks, aviation companies, telecommunications companies, energy firms and government-linked corporations with enormous technical and financial capacity.
The private sector needs to step up
The wrong response to Long Lellang would be to investigate the crash, revise an allowance, purchase or lease several newer helicopters, amend an indemnity form and then declare the problem solved.
The aircraft matters, but the system matters more
This tragedy should not result in the abandonment of the FDS. Quite the opposite. It demonstrates why the service is too important to remain as it is. We need a modern aeromedical service.

People living in Long Lellang, Baram, Kapit, Limbang, and dozens of other remote communities in Peninsular and East Malaysia deserve the same expectation of timely, safe, high-quality care as someone living within minutes of Hospital Kuala Lumpur.
The healthcare workers who volunteer or are assigned to reach them deserve exactly the same commitment to their safety.

We need to ensure that the next generation of Malaysian doctors, nurses, medical assistants and pilots who take to the air to serve rural communities do so as members of a properly trained, insured, equipped, professionally governed and adequately funded aeromedical service.
We owe that to the five people who lost their lives at Long Lellang.
AZRUL MOHD KHALIB
Chief Executive Officer
Galen Centre for Health & Social Policy

8c603b1cbbe76743: JOHOR BARU: Johor has urged the federal government to speed up strategic infrastructure projects crucial to supporting the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), as the state seeks to keep pace with its rapid economic growth.
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said closer coordination with Putrajaya was needed to expedite projects still at the pre-implementation stage, particularly those supporting the JS-SEZ.
He said this during a meeting with Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir, where they discussed Johor's development priorities and the coordination of strategic state and federal projects.

"Every process needs to be streamlined and any issues resolved quickly so project implementation can be accelerated and the benefits felt by Bangsa Johor as soon as possible," Onn Hafiz said in a statement.
He said infrastructure would be critical to the JS-SEZ's competitiveness, investment attraction and creation of jobs and business opportunities.

He said discussions also covered Johor's priorities under the 13th Malaysia Plan, including roads and public transport, housing, healthcare, education, security, coastal management and water resources.

The meeting comes as Johor awaits the JS-SEZ Masterplan and Investment Blueprint, which will provide the broader roadmap for the zone's next phase, including investment priorities, infrastructure enhancements and talent development.
In July, Akmal said the JS-SEZ Masterplan and Investment Blueprint were expected to be launched by December.
The JS-SEZ is a Malaysia-Singapore initiative aimed at deepening economic integration, attracting investment and creating higher-value economic activity in Johor.
Its targets include contributing towards a RM260 billion gross domestic product by 2030 and creating more than 20,000 high-skilled jobs.
c30647366cfe23ab: NEW DELHI: Indian filmmaker Shaunak Sen's new documentary began as a "coping" mechanism after a shock cancer diagnosis, but continues the motifs of environmental degradation and caregiving that drove his previous work.

Sen's All That Breathes, which follows two brothers running a largely self-funded clinic for birds falling victim to Delhi's polluted air, won top documentary prizes at Sundance and Cannes in 2022 and was nominated for Best Documentary Feature at the 2023 Oscars.

"It became a kind of coping strategy, or a way to deal with, dissociate or displace the terror of what you've just been told," Sen, 39, told AFP about his as-yet-untitled project, in an interview from his home in New Delhi.
The diagnosis brought home "the same risks" that make hundreds of birds fall every year from New Delhi's throat-burning polluted skies — this time on "my own body", Sen said.

"Whenever you ask most oncologists why this happened, or why this current giant spike in cancer rates is occurring, a lot of them would talk about environmental factors like toxins or chemicals or the air," he said.

New Delhi and its sprawling metropolitan region of 30 million residents is regularly ranked among the world's most polluted capitals, due to a mix of emissions from power plants, heavy traffic and the burning of rubbish and crops.
A 2024 study in The Lancet Planetary Health estimated that 3.8 million deaths in India between 2009 and 2019 were linked to air pollution.
'MEDITATIVE'
The central protagonist in Sen's new work is not the filmmaker himself but his surgeon.
"I did not want to make something that was solipsistically inwards folding," he said.
It echoes his documentary All That Breathes, where caregiving is at the emotional core of the film.
"What I loved in a surgeon was the ability to completely lose yourself, to be immersed in the absolute present," he said.
"That feels meditative and contemplative. It's a kind of melting away of everything extraneous, and you're in the pinprick of the moment."
CITY AS 'WALLPAPER'
The film is also about Sen's relationship with New Delhi, where he grew up, went to school and university, and the setting for all his work.
"The city," he said, is the "wallpaper of this film."
"In this case, the wallpaper is doing things to me, and I'm kind of reacting to it — through a more personalised lens than I ever have."
His 2016 debut documentary, Cities of Sleep, examined the city's homeless population through the lens of sleep, following them in their quest for a safe place to rest.
Sen is also heading to the Toronto International Film Festival in September to screen Termite, his first fiction short, about two Delhi termite exterminators.
Yet the nature of his latest undertaking means it is inevitably different from his previous work.
Sen's ethnographic approach to filmmaking means shooting characters for long periods to, as he put it, "yield or slow drip certain answers".
"There's a deep pleasure in that kind of a thing," he said.
"Time rewards you with accidents, but in this case, it would be really silly and self-congratulatory for me to say that, 'I gave this film time'."
Sen has had surgery, but continues the long road to recovery.

Shooting the film, he said, was a "way to not look directly at a scary thing", and "to aesthetically convert it into a project, so that you don't have to stare it in the grim eyes of what it actually is".
"I guess it's a kind of a con job."

f1d9ec1bbe8acd9b: JOHOR BARU: Johor will open the country's first non-communicable disease (NCD) clinic in a food court, with six shop lots at Medan Niaga Kampung Melayu Majidee here being converted into a healthcare facility.

State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the RM1 million project, undertaken by the Johor Baru City Council (MBJB), would relocate NCD follow-up services from the Majidee public clinic to the food court.
He said the clinic was expected to serve about 200 patients daily, mainly those requiring follow-up treatment for hypertension, high cholesterol and diabetes.
"Once completed, this is expected to be the first NCD clinic in Malaysia operating within a food court," he said.
The six existing lots will be refurbished into treatment rooms and equipped with air-conditioning, furniture and medical equipment.
Ling said MBJB was undertaking the tender and procurement process, while renovation works were expected to take three to four months.
The clinic is targeted to begin operations early next year.
The initiative is aimed at bringing follow-up NCD services closer to the community and easing access to healthcare.
Meanwhile, to ease pressure on the public clinic in Mengkibol in Kluang, which sees more than 1,000 patients daily, several measures have been introduced.
Ling said the congestion was after some NCD follow-up services were transferred from the Enche' Besar Hajjah Khalsom Hospital to the clinic due to manpower shortages.

The Mengkibol clinic, the only government health facility providing comprehensive services in central Kluang, has faced tighter space, congestion and longer waiting times as patients with hypertension, diabetes and high cholesterol were redirected there.

Ling said immediate measures taken include scheduled appointments, extended service hours and relocating blood-taking services to a former dining hall in an adjacent building, which have improved patient flow to some extent.
Further proposals, including wider use of electronic queue management and decanting some services to a more suitable location, are being assessed with the Johor Health Department, he said.
49f7a4d3e9f6a30f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Malaysia’s total palm oil stocks rose by 196,590 tonnes, or 7.48 per cent, to 2.82 million tonnes in August 2026 from 2.62 million tonnes a month earlier, according to the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB).
MPOB said crude palm oil (CPO) stocks increased 15.20 per cent, or 217,092 tonnes, to 1.64 million tonnes in August 2026 from 1.42 million tonnes in July 2026.
“However, processed palm oil stockpiles eased 1.71 per cent to 1.17 million tonnes from 1.19 million tonnes in July,” it said in its Malaysian Palm Oil Industry, August 2026, performance report.

On production, MPOB said CPO output increased 1.39 per cent, or 24,903 tonnes, to 1.81 million tonnes from 1.79 million a month earlier, while palm kernel output also rose 1.97 per cent month-on-month to 430,599 tonnes from 422,272 tonnes.
Crude palm kernel oil production increased 0.10 per cent to 199,589 tonnes from 199,392 tonnes in July, while palm kernel cake output climbed 0.25 per cent to 215,847 tonnes from 215,304 tonnes.

MPOB said palm oil exports declined 7.50 per cent in August 2026 to 1.29 million tonnes from 1.39 million tonnes a month earlier. Palm kernel oil exports rose by 37.22 per cent to 112,879 tonnes from 82,261 tonnes a month ago. Palm kernel cake exports also expanded by 6.45 per cent to 216,584 tonnes from 203,454 tonnes.
Meanwhile, oleochemical exports fell 12.72 per cent to 233,545 tonnes from 267,576 tonnes in July, while biodiesel exports surged by 22.59 per cent to 35,240 tonnes from 28,745 tonnes last month.

MPOB reported zero CPO imports in August. Processed palm oil and palm oil were both down 0.09 per cent to 49,524 tonnes from 49,566 tonnes in July. August’s palm kernel oil imports rose 21.14 per cent to 13,985 tonnes, from 11,545 tonnes in the preceding month. — Bernama
efa1ee9c9e3eabd4: KLUANG: Neighbours desperately tried to save a family of three trapped in a burning two-storey terrace house at Taman Titiwangsa here last night, with some even climbing onto the roof before being forced back by the intense heat.
Neighbour Jaafar Hussin, 57, said the fire spread rapidly from the ground floor, leaving them little time to reach the victims on the upper floor. All three died.
Jaafar was having a drink at a nearby shop with the victims' father, Khairul Nizam Wahid, 50, before they returned home on their motorcycles at 10.30pm.
"Khairul Nizam said he had a stomach ache and went inside. When he opened the door, he shouted, 'My house is on fire'.
"I saw the sofa burning. He tried to pull it out, but the fire spread rapidly.
"We told his wife and children to open the upstairs windows and get out," he said when met today.
Jaafar said several neighbours, including three Pakistanis, tried to reach the family by climbing onto the roof but had to turn back because of the intense heat.
"Others brought buckets of water and opened their house taps to fight the fire, but we could not put it out," he said.
Jaafar said he had known the family for more than 20 years and described them as close friends.
"They were like family to us. They run a catering business and neighbours would help whenever they received orders," he said.
Meanwhile, post-mortems on Noraini Ibrahim, 49, and her two sons, Khairul Nurhaziqq Khairulnizam, 18, and Khairul Nurhadif, 11, were still being conducted at Enche' Besar Hajjah Khalsom Hospital.
The bodies were expected to be claimed by relatives later today for burial in a single grave at the Kampung Bentong Dalam Muslim cemetery after Asar.
The three bodies were found by firefighters. They had been trapped in a room upstairs.

e09c556ce7bc7679: SINGAPORE, Sept 10 — A Singapore family court has granted a man a personal protection order against his wife after finding that her messages and AI-generated fake images and videos depicting him having sex with his sister amounted to family violence.

CNA reported that Magistrate Soh Kian Peng found the man had suffered emotional or psychological abuse after his wife repeatedly accused him of having a sexual relationship with his sister, with the couple’s strained relationship also involving the woman’s acrimonious ties with her sister-in-law.

The man told the court that the dispute began after he agreed to contribute S$100,000 (US$79,120) towards his father’s medical expenses and informed his wife that he had transferred about S$65,000 to his sister.
The wife responded with messages that Soh described as “hideously offensive and vile”, while the husband was evidently “tormented and distressed” during the trial.
The court heard that the husband submitted 90 pages of screenshots showing messages from his wife as well as explicit AI-generated images and videos of him and his sister.
The wife did not deny sending the material and said she had used a free application to create the obscene images and videos.
Soh said it was “abundantly clear” that the messages and images had inflicted emotional or psychological abuse on the man, who had lost weight “precipitously”.

The magistrate found that the husband had established both grounds required for a protection order in a family setting, namely that his wife had committed family violence against him and that an order was necessary for his protection or personal safety.
Soh also found a high risk that the wife would continue the abuse, noting that she had stopped sending such messages only after the husband applied for the order.

The magistrate said the dispute involving the sister-in-law remained unresolved and that it was not realistic to expect the husband to cut off all contact with his sister to avoid conflict with his wife.
He added that while the wife might have had her own grievances and frustrations with her husband, she did not have a healthy way of expressing those emotions.

Besides granting the protection order, Soh directed the couple to attend counselling and ordered a preliminary assessment report on the wife, who had been admitted to the Institute of Mental Health twice, with a view to possible mandatory treatment for a psychiatric condition.
41b8e3eb245674dd: KUALA LUMPUR: Cape EMS Bhd, via subsidiary Cape Renewables Sdn Bhd, is partnering with Helios PV (Asia Pacific) Pte Ltd to market and distribute Malaysian-assembled home battery storage systems (BESS).
The systems will be sold across Europe and Asia Pacific, expanding Cape EMS's reach in the fast-growing energy-storage market.
Cape EMS will leverage its manufacturing facility in Senai, Johor for the sourcing, localising, system integration, assembly, testing and supplying residential BESS solutions.

"Helios, backed by more than 15 years of experience in solar system integration, will spearhead market development, importation, distribution and first-level customer support," it said in a statement.
Germany has been identified as the initial strategic market for the residential BESS solutions before the companies progressively expand into the wider European Union.
Cape EMS said this is due to the nation's mature battery storage market and growing adoption of integrated solar generation and energy storage.

"The vast majority of these storage systems operate alongside photovoltaic infrastructure, demonstrating the increasingly important role of integrated solar generation and energy storage in modern residential energy consumption.
"This provides Cape EMS with a clear strategic entry point into the European residential energy storage value chain," it said.

Cape EMS said as European customers increasingly prioritise supply-chain diversification, product traceability and regulatory compliance, the company is positioning Malaysia as a credible alternative manufacturing and system integration base for the European market.
"This positioning is becoming increasingly relevant as Europe strengthens regulatory frameworks surrounding battery lifecycle accountability," it added.
2dcedb7a21eb23c8: MARAN: Twenty-one patients, including 11 children, who were evacuated following a ceiling fire at Jengka Hospital's paediatric ward yesterday have been transferred to other hospitals.
The Pahang Health Department said that healthcare services at the hospital remain uninterrupted, with affected patients moved to Jerantut Hospital and Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital in Temerloh.
In a statement, the department said the 7pm fire was confined to the paediatric ward, and firefighters extinguished the blaze before it could spread.
No patients or accompanying family members were injured.

"Due to renovation works at Jengka Hospital's women's ward, adult female patients were temporarily housed in the paediatric ward. At the time of the fire, there were 11 children accompanied by 11 family members, alongside 10 female patients.

"The department transferred 10 female patients and three children to Jerantut Hospital, while eight children were taken to the Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital to ensure their medical care continues seamlessly."
Yesterday's fire forced the evacuation of occupants from the paediatric ward. The fire is believed to have started in the roof section above the ward, with the exact cause still under investigation.
Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said firefighters extinguished the blaze within 20 minutes, adding that about 10 per cent of the ceiling was damaged.

08072898f2856b8c: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno’s women’s youth wing, Puteri Umno, today extended its best wishes for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency bid ahead of a meeting expected to discuss his application.
This follows a report by Free Malaysia Today that the Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss Najib’s clemency application during its meeting this week.
Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi expressed the wing’s positive wishes during a press conference at the Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL) today.
“And we always prayed for the eased of everything,” Amal said.
Amal met local media after delivering her keynote address at the Puteri Umno General Assembly at WTCKL.

FMT had also previously reported that Najib’s application was expected to be among the issues raised at the board’s meeting, although it remained unclear whether the meeting would result in a decision or merely a discussion.
It also reported that Najib could potentially be allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, although it was unclear whether the option would be considered at the meeting.
Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine.
He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
The Pardons Board subsequently halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
On Dec 22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest. Najib later withdrew his appeal against the decision.
bc0fc982d89d5fcd: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno never questioned the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's prerogative to grant Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim a full royal pardon, said its Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh.
Dr Akmal said the party had also pursued official channels following former Umno president Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conviction, without accusing the courts of acting unfairly.
"When the court punished Najib, we were upset but never said the courts were acting unfairly or challenged it. Instead, we pursued legal channels because we respect the courts.
"Even when Anwar received a royal pardon, we never questioned the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's prerogative," he said in his policy speech at the Umno Youth delegates' conference here today.

Anwar, now prime minister and Pakatan Harapan chairman, was imprisoned in 1998 and again in 2015. He received a full royal pardon from Sultan Muhammad V after PH won the 14th General Election in 2018.
Yesterday, Umno criticised the PH secretariat council over a statement that it said pre-empted the Pardons Board's consideration.
The PH secretariat council had said those convicted of corruption or abuse of power, particularly in high-profile cases, should serve their full court sentences.
Without naming anyone, it backed the government's anti-corruption efforts and the King's call for thorough, uncompromising investigations.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki accused PH of questioning the King's pardon powers, saying these were His Majesty's prerogative under Article 42(1) of the Federal Constitution.
He questioned why others should face a different standard when PH had supported Anwar's pardon before he completed his sentence.

Earlier today, PKR Youth information chief Danish Hairudin urged Asyraf to clarify his allegation, saying PH had made no such statement and had instead raised concerns about corruption, abuse of power, court sentences and the rule of law.
d32ba8a2b3548206: KUALA LUMPUR: George Town in Penang has been awarded the Silver Award at the second Asean Smoke-free Awards, recognising its achievements in implementing and enforcing smoke-free policies to protect public health.
The awards were presented today during the opening ceremony of the 17th Asean Health Ministers' Meeting here.
The initiative is led by the Laotian government under the Asean Health Cluster 1, in cooperation with the Southeast Asia Tobacco Control Alliance (SEATCA) and the Asean Secretariat.
Baguio City in the Philippines took the Gold Award, while five local governments from Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines and Thailand received Bronze Awards.
Singapore received a Special Recognition certificate for its consistent and outstanding smoke-free enforcement.
SEATCA executive director Dr Ulysses Dorotheo said the awards demonstrated that strict and firmly enforced smoke-free policies were both achievable and necessary in the fight against tobacco.
"This year's awardees demonstrate that strict and firmly enforced smoke-free policies are achievable and necessary if millions of lives are to be saved from the deadly tobacco epidemic," he said.
He said SEATCA would continue working with the awarded cities to build on their achievements, and expressed confidence that other governments in the region would draw inspiration from their example.

"Local governments are demonstrating that smoke-free environments can and must become the standard all over the region by firmly resisting challenges from the tobacco industry and by placing public health first," he said.
The Laotian Health Ministry said the second edition of the awards reflected the region's shared commitment to translating high-level Asean commitments into real protections for its people.
The Asean Smoke-free Awards builds on the "Towards a Smoke-free Asean" campaign initiated in March 2012 at the World Conference on Tobacco or Health in Singapore.
The inaugural ceremony was held in Vientiane, Laos in August 2024, when Iloilo City in the Philippines received the first-ever Gold Award.

c9b30a27c1a2042b: SEOUL: South Korea's president has ruled out even considering to extend his constitutionally-capped one term in office, a spokesman said Thursday, after the leader and some allies had floated a reform.

President Lee Jae Myung's critics noted a second term would extend the suspension of five criminal trials against him, including on bribery charges linked to a firm's alleged illicit transfer of US$8 million to North Korea.

South Korea adopted its current single five-year presidential term in 1987 as the country transitioned from decades of authoritarian rule, in part to prevent the prolonged concentration of presidential power.
Lee said on social media in August that he favoured a four-year presidency allowing for more than one term, while shifting some presidential powers to parliament.

National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik, formerly affiliated with Lee's Democratic Party, said in July that voters should decide whether an incumbent president could seek another term under a revised constitution.
Speaking to South Koreans in Paris on Wednesday during a state visit to France, Lee noted he has just one term.
"My term is clearly limited under the constitution, so the earlier we start, the longer we can enjoy the benefits," Lee said, explaining why he had scheduled many overseas visits.

Seong Ghi-hong, senior presidential secretary for public relations and communication, said Lee's remarks should be understood as ruling out any attempt to seek re-election through a constitutional amendment.

"I interpret his remarks to mean that the idea of a consecutive term – which is being discussed in some quarters – is completely impossible and not even a matter for consideration," he told a radio programme in South Korea.
Since Cho's remarks, the opposition People Power Party has accused Lee and his allies of considering an amendment that could allow him to remain in office.
Proposals to allow presidents to serve more than one term have repeatedly emerged since the 1987 revision of the constitution, but those attempts have failed amid political opposition.
Lee's remarks come as his approval rating has fallen to its lowest level since he took office, with a Gallup Korea poll released last week putting it at 40 per cent.

c4c12739011fcc32: ATHENS, Sept 10 — A Greek woman has given birth from an embryo frozen over 22 years ago, months after her son born from the same treatment in 2004 died in an accident, her doctor said Wednesday.
“For Christina Rapti‑Tzelepi, today’s birth carries special emotional significance,” gynaecologist Konstantinos Pantos said in a Facebook post.

“In 2004, after an embryo transfer, she had a healthy baby boy on the first attempt. In October 2025, the family experienced the tragic loss of their son in a road traffic accident at the age of 21,” Pantos said.
Rapti-Tzelepi is 54, the maximum allowed age in Greece for in vitro fertilisation.
She gave birth to a baby girl on Wednesday following the transfer in December of an embryo from the same initial batch, Pantos said.
“There was mourning and joy involved, but everything disappeared this morning when we held our beauty in our arms,” Rapti-Tzelepi told state TV ERT.
Rapti-Tzelepi’s husband Konstantinos Raptis said the family were in a “race against time” to see the pregnancy through.
“My wife reached, quite literally, the very limits of the age restrictions imposed by the existing legislation,” Raptis said in a statement.
He called for the national IVF age limit to be lifted.
“Older women have an immeasurable capacity to offer mature, conscious and unconditional love, as well as a stability that no statistic can ever fully measure,” Raptis said.
The couple have an additional nine embryos in storage and would like to have another child, but are currently unable to under the law, Pantos said.
Greece’s birth rate has been declining for years. State statistics in 2025 showed births had fallen by over 2,800 compared to a year earlier.
However, the data also shows an increase in births to mothers over the age of 40 over the past 20 years.
“Women must not be afraid... the science is safe... I advise couples that have been fighting for years to not give up,” Rapti-Tzelepi said.
“In a country with a serious birth rate problem, we must not deprive people of their dreams and desires.” — AFP
9bef32d4c5a930c3: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today he will meet Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim during the party’s general assembly to seek an explanation over his statement regarding a proclamation involving the state’s ruler.

f5241e65b16aec6e: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said he was hoping for the best when the Pardons Board considers former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency bid tomorrow.
Zahid reiterated today that the power of the pardon was constitutionally vested in the Yang diPertuan Agong.

“I am confident that His Majesty’s discretion and wisdom will determine the final decision, which is His Majesty’s absolute prerogative to announce,” he told reporters at the Umno general assembly here.
The Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss Najib’s latest application for tomorrow.

FMT reported that sources familiar with the matter said Najib’s application was expected to be among the issues raised at the board’s meeting, although it remained unclear whether the meeting would result in a decision or merely a discussion.

A separate source told the online news portal that Najib could potentially be allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, although it was unclear whether the option would be considered at the meeting.

Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine. He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
In 2024, the Pardons Board halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
However, Najib and his lawyers subsequently insisted that the partial pardon came with a royal addendum for him to serve out his remaining time at home, eventually suing to have this granted.

On Dec 22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest. Najib withdrew his appeal against the decision in April this year.
93243d9544ebeea5: KUALA LUMPUR: Presiden Umno Zahid Hamidi menyerahkan sepenuhnya keputusan berhubung nasib Najib Razak kepada kebijaksanaan Yang di-Pertuan Agong menjelang Mesyuarat Lembaga Pengampunan esok.

b3f4df18fbf90508: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today presented instruments of appointment to two judges at Istana Negara.
The ceremony began with the presentation to Court of Appeal judge Alice Loke Yee Ching, followed by High Court judge Elaine Yap Chin Gaik.

Present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, Court of Appeal President Datuk Seri Abu Bakar Jais, Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah and Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi.
Loke, 64, was appointed Senior Federal Counsel in 2013, a position she held until 2018. She was appointed a judicial commissioner of the Shah Alam High Court on July 10, 2020.
She was elevated to Shah Alam High Court judge on Jan 17, 2023, before being appointed to the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s Special Powers Division on Aug 18, 2025.

As a Kuala Lumpur High Court judge, Loke handled Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak’s judicial review application over an alleged addendum order allowing the former prime minister to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.

During her tenure as Senior Federal Counsel, Loke was involved in several high-profile cases, including admiralty proceedings at the Kuala Lumpur High Court to seize the Equanimity, a vessel allegedly built using funds from 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB).
She also handled the Sulu claim and lawsuits filed against the Malaysian government over the disappearance of Malaysia Airlines flight MH370.
Meanwhile, Yap, 53, holds a Bachelor of Laws from the University of Sydney and a Diploma in International Arbitration from the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators.
She was appointed a judicial commissioner of the Shah Alam High Court on Aug 28, 2024, before taking up the same position at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on Nov 3, 2025. — Bernama
cdd978a1ede45073: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno Youth is ready to support a proposed mega ummah unity gathering with PAS as part of efforts to strengthen Malay-Muslim political cooperation.

Wing chief Dr Akmal Saleh said the initiative, proposed by PAS Youth chief Afnan Hamimi Taib Azamudden at the Islamic party's recent muktamar, should go beyond a gathering and lead to concrete discussions and solutions for young Malays.

"In his policy speech, Afnan called for a mega ummah unity gathering. Today, Umno Youth responds – we are ready to answer that call," Akmal said in his policy speech at the Umno Youth assembly at World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur today.
He said Umno Youth would discuss the future of the Malay community and seek practical solutions for young Malays through the wing's Rimbun or national roundtable discussion initiative.
He said the ideas and spirit of the initiative would then be brought nationwide through an ummah unity roadshow.
Akmal said Umno and PAS did not need to abandon their identities for their cooperation to succeed.
"Umno remains Umno and PAS remains PAS. Mature unity does not require us to discard our identities – it requires us to manage our differences with wisdom," he said.
He also dismissed suggestions that his efforts to strengthen ties with PAS amounted to seeking a new political ally.
"Some say we are flirting and starting to look for a (new) partner. I want to answer frankly: we did not go looking for new love. We went looking for common ground for the nation’s future," he said.
Akmal also said efforts to unite the two Malay-Muslim political forces should not be derailed by past disagreements.
He acknowledged that the initiative had drawn criticism, including personal attacks against him.
"But I will not bow to pressure, I will not turn back and I will not compromise on this ummah unity," he said.

bf7f28d443f04721: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno's political cooperation should be assessed based on the dynamics and realities of each state, rather than through a one-size-fits-all approach, said a Penang Wanita Umno delegate.

Speaking while supporting a motion at the Wanita Umno general assembly today, Nibong Tebal chief Siti Hawa Mohd Nordin said Malaysian politics had become increasingly fragmented, with shifting voter loyalties and uncertain support making every election a different battleground.
She said Umno must remain firm on its principles while being flexible in its political strategy, particularly when deciding whether to cooperate with other parties or contest on its own.

Siti Hawa proposed that the party's central leadership set the principles and red lines, while state Umno liaison bodies be given room to propose political formulas based on their respective states' realities.
She said decisions must also be explained to the grassroots, who are members who worked on the ground daily and during elections.
"Cooperation that is not understood will look like an elite arrangement. Cooperation that is explained honestly can become a shared struggle," she said.
Citing Sabah, Johor and Negri Sembilan as examples, she said the different political approaches taken in the three states showed that no single formula could be applied nationwide.
"Three states, three approaches.
"What is the lesson? Not every form of cooperation brings victory, and not every solo approach is suitable everywhere," she said.
She said the Sabah formula could not simply be copied in Johor, just as the Johor approach could not be imposed on Negeri Sembilan.
"Politics is not about guessing; it is about reading the ground," she said.
Siti Hawa said Umno had several options because it still had its roots, experience, machinery and bargaining power.
"Having several options is not a sign of lacking principles. It means we cannot be forced to accept a path that disadvantages the party and the people," she said.
On Penang, Siti Hawa said Umno could not depend on a single stream of votes given the state's demographic and political makeup.
She said the party must strengthen Malay confidence while building acceptance across communities, adding that Umno needed to remain present beyond elections by addressing issues affecting the rakyat.
"Cooperation must not turn Umno into a passenger in a house that we also helped build," she said.
Siti Hawa said Umno must be seen as a respected partner rather than merely a vehicle for transferring Malay votes to other parties.
She said the party should also be prepared to contest on its own, build understandings with other parties or serve as a strong and principled opposition if fair terms could not be achieved.
"A party that has only one option can easily be pressured. A party prepared with several paths can negotiate with its head held high," she said.
Siti Hawa also called for women to be given a greater role in decision-making, particularly in candidate selection and the administration of the country.

She said Umno's Constitution must be amended to guarantee at least 30 per cent women candidates for parliamentary and state assembly seats, rather than confining them to positions within the party's wings or placing them in seats that are difficult to win.
She said the guarantee must cover at least 30 per cent of seats currently held by Umno or those with potential to be won, stressing that the figure should be regarded as a floor, not a ceiling.
"Even the most sophisticated political strategy will falter if women are asked to work but are not given space to make decisions," she said.
"We do not want women's energy to be used during campaigns while their voices are diminished when candidates are selected," she said.

d73cb149fa87b8b5: NEW YORK: Alexander Zverev took another big step towards a second Grand Slam title by beating Dutchman Botic van de Zandschulp 6-2 7-5 6-1 to reach the US Open semi-finals, where the German will take on Karen Khachanov.
The 29-year-old French Open champion got off to a slow start in his campaign at Flushing Meadows but has steadily found his range.
"I think you saw in the first two rounds, I really didn't play well," Zverev said.

"In other tournaments I would be out in the first round, but here I can fight back and play best of five sets, play 4-1/2 hours. I've started playing better throughout the tournament and I'm definitely happy to be in the semi-finals here."
The German has reached the semi-finals at all four majors this year and is the only Grand Slam winner left standing in the men's draw.
"I don't take it for granted at all," Zverev said.
"I know it can change in a heartbeat in tennis. I think confidence is something that is incredibly important but also can go away quite quickly."

Zverev was far from steady on serve early on at Arthur Ashe Stadium, coughing up five double faults in an erratic start, but van de Zandschulp leaked forehand errors to allow the top seed to break in the fifth game and then take the first set.

Van de Zandschulp regrouped in the second set and came close to levelling the contest, but Zverev absorbed the pressure and reeled off three games in a row towards the end as the momentum swung firmly in the German's favour.
Zverev, the 2020 runner-up, fired an overhead smash to break early in the third set and cruised home from there to reach his third semi-final in New York.
With 23 Grand Slam match wins this year, Zverev surpassed Boris Becker's German men's record of 22 from 1989.
He next faces Russian Khachanov in a rematch of their gold medal showdown at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021. - Reuters
1b261dcfcce5818d: SEOUL: Leader Kim Jong Un praised troops in "overseas military operations" during a speech marking North Korea's founding anniversary, state media reported Thursday, an apparent nod to Pyongyang's assistance in Moscow's war against Ukraine.

Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, North Korea has become a key ally of the Kremlin, sending troops to support Moscow's war effort in return for economic benefits and military technology, analysts say.

During comments marking North Korea's Sept 9, 1948 founding, Kim hailed overseas compatriots but paid special tribute to troops deployed abroad, the official Korean Central News Agency reported on Thursday.
"I also extend my special gratitude and profound respect to the commanders and soldiers of our military participating in overseas military operations," said Kim on the nation's the 78th anniversary.
"Our ideal is being realised rapidly thanks to patriotism, voluntary service and devoted contributions by all citizens praying for the country's prosperity," he added.
According to South Korea, some 2,000 North Korean troops have been killed in the war between Russia and Ukraine.
In August, Ukraine claimed that Moscow had launched North Korean ballistic missiles in a strike that killed at least nine people and wounded dozens.
Kyiv has also said that up to 50,000 North Korean troops are due to deploy to Russia, although it has provided no evidence to back the claim or a timeframe for the deployment.
In making the claim, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy asked Seoul to supply air defence systems to protect against Russian missiles, a request that has gone unanswered by the South.
62cd646bd0ebd773: IPOH, September 10 — The Perak Legislative Assembly today approved the appointment of Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri as a senator after he secured 33 votes in a secret ballot.

1442181dbb154832: KUALA LUMPUR: Layang Layang Aerospace secara sukarela menggantung sementara perkhidmatan helikopter jenis BO-105 serta pesawat lain yang dilengkapi enjin Rolls-Royce 250 susulan nahas berhampiran STOLport Long Lellang di Sarawak.

Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Pihak Berkuasa Penerbangan Awam Malaysia (CAAM), Norazman Mahmud, berkata langkah penggantungan itu merupakan tindakan pencegahan keselamatan diambil sendiri pihak pengendali, dan bukannya petanda kemalangan berkenaan disebabkan kerosakan enjin atau teknikal.

Mengulas kebimbangan awam berhubung usia pesawat tersebut, Norazman menegaskan faktor usia semata-mata bukanlah penentu kepada tahap keselamatan penerbangan, selagi mana pesawat diselenggara dengan betul dan memenuhi piawaian kelayakan udara yang ditetapkan.

Beliau berkata, pihak CAAM sedang memantau proses penggantungan operasi dan pemeriksaan oleh pengendali berkenaan, selain menyemak semula rekod kawal selia bagi pesawat, syarikat pengendali, dan juga juruterbang.
"Siasatan bebas berhubung nahas itu diketuai oleh Biro Siasatan Kemalangan Udara (BSKU) di bawah Kementerian Pengangkutan," katanya selepas menghadiri Seminar Keselamatan Penerbangan Malaysia 2026.

Beliau juga menasihatkan semua pihak tidak membuat sebarang spekulasi mengenai punca insiden sama ada berpunca daripada kerosakan teknikal, faktor cuaca, mahupun kesilapan manusia, sambil menekankan sebarang keputusan muktamad hanya akan dikeluarkan BSKU.
a0b49fa725847622: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno Youth has assured non-Malays and non-Muslims that the ummah unity agenda proposed jointly with Pas poses no threat to them or their rights.

Its chief, Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, said the wing was ready to defend the party's commitment to the agenda and ensure it benefited everyone, instead of remaining confined to political discussions.

"Defending Malays does not mean being hostile towards non-Malays, while upholding Islam does not mean denying the rights of followers of other faiths, because Islam teaches us that strong leadership must be fair to all," he said in his policy speech at the Umno Youth delegates' conference here today.
Akmal said Barisan Nasional's track record demonstrated this, with MCA, MIC and Parti Bersatu Rakyat Sabah retaining their respective Chinese, Indian and Bumiputera identities within the coalition.
Akmal, who is also a Merlimau assemblyman, said Umno should neither be ashamed nor afraid to acknowledge Pas as another major Malay-Muslim political force.
"Acknowledging this reality does not diminish Umno's role in any way. Instead, it shows our courage in facing reality.
"Developments in Johor and Negri Sembilan also prove that Umno and Pas can support each other when the interests of the ummah are placed above rivalry," he said.
However, he said political unity should not be measured merely by seat numbers, power negotiations or enthusiasm on the political stage, but by tangible improvements in people's lives.

"Unity must reach the people's dining tables because, ultimately, they do not want to see who sits at the same table, but what reaches their dining tables," he added.
1a35c979574c3669: TOKYO: A landslide struck a car park on Japan's Mount Fuji, with the final day of the volcano's summer climbing season on Thursday marred by downpours and dense mist.
Three vehicles belonging to people working on the mountain were partially buried Wednesday, as powerful gusts and torrential rain battered the popular hiking destination, a local official told AFP.

No injuries were reported in the incident, which occurred in a parking lot at one of the 3,776-metre volcano's four main access gates, said Hisayuki Motohashi, a road maintenance official for the Shizuoka regional government.
Separately, Shizuoka police said on Thursday they had been called to help rescue two hikers.

A man who appeared to be in his 30s or 40s was found collapsed near the summit Wednesday while another man who appeared to be in his 60s was found fallen on a trail the same day, according to a local police official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
She did not provide details about the condition of both individuals.
The local Shizuoka government and official mountain guides posted video clips and photos from the mountain Thursday morning, showing access roads and gravel trails covered with dense mist and rain.
Mount Fuji attracts more than 200,000 hikers every year during its official opening period from July through September.
Local police rescue dozens of people and report a few deaths every year.
In recent years, communities around the popular mountain have tightened access rules to Mount Fuji to ease severe overtourism problems.
They have also tried to stop poorly equipped climbers from summitting and mandating that visitors spend at least one night at one of the huts on the trails.
On Tuesday, hundreds of Asian Games athletes in Japan were briefly evacuated from their accommodation as record rainfall lashed host city Nagoya.
4fd2fb8c680e84d0: LONDON: Britain is heading into winter with soaring gas prices, high household bills and a slim fuel buffer to cushion it from another energy shock that could stoke inflation.

UK gas prices have climbed to their highest since 2022 and more than doubled since the start of the year, just as households face the highest winter energy costs in three years. The combination risks reigniting the cost-of-living squeeze and piling pressure on the government to protect consumers.

Britain is particularly exposed because it relies heavily on gas while storing little of its own, leaving it dependent on seaborne liquefied natural gas when demand surges or renewable generation falters. The war in the Middle East has deepened that vulnerability, with Qatari LNG flows disrupted, intensifying competition for fuel just as Europe tries to rebuild depleted inventories.

Its gas storage capacity is equivalent to just 12 days of average winter demand, compared with three to four months in Germany and France. That thin buffer could shrink further if the government decides not to support Rough, the country’s largest gas storage site. Operator Centrica Plc has warned it could close permanently without a deal in the coming months.

The conflict “is dragging us back into the ominous territory of wholesale gas prices last seen in 2022, which - alongside high oil prices - are pushing up bills and driving wider inflation,” said Simon Cran-McGreehin, head of analysis at the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit.

That leaves prime minister Andy Burnham under pressure to soften the blow, with bills expected to rise further in October and again in January. The Treasury will scrap the 5% value-added tax on energy bills from October, though the benefit is expected to be largely wiped out by a 4% increase in the price cap.

The government is also considering extending its £150 (US$204) Warm Home Discount to more households, Bloomberg reported. Consumer groups have warned the relief may be too limited for those who fall outside existing means-tested support.

At the same time, Burnham’s government is set to announce new North Sea gas drilling next week, including approval for the controversial Jackdaw field off Aberdeen, according to people familiar with the matter.

But new domestic production offers little immediate protection. Britain’s gas market is tied to Europe and global LNG prices, meaning UK producers generally sell at prevailing market rates - leaving the government with few quick ways to shield households if the rally persists.
8a1af5235a9f30e6: KUALA LUMPUR: Hockey legend Datuk Seri N. Sri Shanmuganathan was discharged from the National Heart Institute (IJN) on Monday as he recovers at home.

The 79-year-old Olympian and World Cupper Shanmuganathan said that consultant cardiologist Datuk Dr Kumara Gurupparan Ganesan informed him that there is a problem in his main artery.
"I am given medication for a month. I had surgery to remove three blocks two years ago and I am too old to do another open-heart surgery.

"I was discharged from hospital on Monday and two nurses from IJN home care service came this morning to my house to check on my condition," said Shanmuganathan, who captained Malaysia to a creditable fourth place in the 1975 World Cup in Kuala Lumpur.
Shanmuganathan said he is concerned about Brian's condition.
"Brian will be in the hospital for another one week," he said.
Brian, who is also suffering from Parkinson's disease, had a fall at his home on Aug 29 and was then hospitalised.
The 76-year-old Brian's condition worsened after he was unable to get up on his own. His recovery had been slow and he is still struggling to walk.
8c43e94a484cbde4: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Bangi member of parliament Dr Ong Kian Ming says tensions with DAP began after an influencer shared slides from a private briefing in which he predicted Pakatan Harapan would suffer a major defeat in the Johor election.

Speaking on the latest episode of the Keluar Sekejap podcast, he said the forecast was initially shared privately with journalists at the briefing, before becoming public once an influencer obtained a copy of his presentation slides.
"The prediction was not something I made to bring down PH or run down DAP," he said, adding that DAP leaders at the time asked why he had made it.
Ong said DAP's unhappiness over the episode, coupled with the party's failure to engage with him about his predictions, contributed to his decision to quit the party.

He said he made a similar prediction about the Negri Sembilan election, including that DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke could lose the Chennah seat, an eventuality that came to pass as Loke lost to Barisan Nasional's Siow Kong Choon by 688 votes.
"Not because he didn't serve well, but because the political wind blowing was very strong," he said, describing a strong anti-PH political current and an ummah unity narrative.
He said no DAP leader had reached out to question his predictions or ask how his analysis could help the party prepare for future state or general elections.
"I think that's also a signal to me that they're uncomfortable with me, but at the same time, they also feel there's no need to engage with me," he said.

Ong resigned from DAP on Aug 31, ruling out joining another party or contesting the 16th General Election, while reaffirming his pledge to campaign for former health minister Khairy Jamaluddin if he is fielded as a candidate.
An analyst later told the New Straits Times Ong's exit raises questions over DAP's ability to retain talent such as his.
Ong joined DAP in 2012 and served as its assistant political education director.
He also served as deputy international trade and industry minister under Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad's PH government between 2018 and 2020.
Ong said that in the two weeks after he informed the party of his decision to leave, no one, including Loke, contacted him to try and persuade him to stay.
"So I also saw this as a signal that this was a good date to announce DAP's independence from me, and my independence from DAP," he said.
He also said his marginalisation in DAP had been developing for years, not overnight.
He said losing the party's central executive committee election in 2022 was a signal that professionals such as himself and former DAP leader Tony Pua had "outstayed our welcome" in the party.
Pua lost the Selangor chapter's election and was not included in the state committee, before both he and Ong lost the CEC election.
Ong said he had already decided not to contest the 2022 general election before losing the CEC election.
"Because I made that decision, I also felt I could advise the then DAP secretary-general, Lim Guan Eng, not to take up the position of chairman in DAP.
"I think that was perhaps the beginning of the end of my career in DAP," he said.

He said he had already identified Syahredzan Johan as someone who could eventually replace him as Bangi MP but continued to hold on to hope that he would play a role in DAP after the 2022 election, particularly on policy matters.
"But that was something that DAP and its leaders perhaps felt they were smarter or more knowledgeable about than I was," he said.
"So I'm okay with that because I also have roles and responsibilities to play in other arenas."

f758ffb2b8fc6767: PETALING JAYA: A Kuala Lumpur DAP leader has called on party members in the Cabinet to resign in the event that former prime minister Najib Razak, who is currently serving time for a graft conviction, is pardoned.
Ben Fong said it would be "untenable" for DAP to remain in government if Najib is released.
"This is a red line that we cannot cross," Fong, the Kuala Lumpur DAP treasurer, said in a statement.

It was reported that the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) is expected to meet tomorrow to consider, among other matters, Najib's bid for a pardon of his convictions linked to the 1MDB scandal.

Najib, 72, was convicted six years ago of misappropriating RM42 million in SRC International funds. He was fined RM210 million and handed a 12-year jail term which he has been serving at Kajang prison since August 2022.
The FTPB later halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.

In December 2025, Najib was convicted of abuse of power and money laundering involving over RM2 billion linked to 1MDB. He was sentenced to 15 years’ jail and fined RM11.38 billion. He is appealing the conviction.
Fong said that leaving the Cabinet did not necessarily mean bringing down the government.
He said DAP could continue supporting the government from outside the Cabinet to preserve political stability and push for institutional reforms.
"But stability cannot become an excuse for accepting everything. Political leaders must recognise that some lines cannot be crossed."
There are five ministers and seven deputy ministers from DAP in Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s administration.
239be917d6f15ae2: SEOUL, Sept 10 — South Korea’s president has ruled out even considering to extend his constitutionally-capped one term in office, a spokesman said Thursday, after the leader and some allies had floated a reform.

President Lee Jae Myung’s critics noted a second term would extend the suspension of five criminal trials against him, including on bribery charges linked to a firm’s alleged illicit transfer of US$8 million (RM32.5 million) to North Korea.

South Korea adopted its current single five-year presidential term in 1987 as the country transitioned from decades of authoritarian rule, in part to prevent the prolonged concentration of presidential power.
Lee said on social media in August that he favoured a four-year presidency allowing for more than one term, while shifting some presidential powers to parliament.

National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik, formerly affiliated with Lee’s Democratic Party, said in July that voters should decide whether an incumbent president could seek another term under a revised constitution.
Speaking to South Koreans in Paris on Wednesday during a state visit to France, Lee noted he has just one term.
“My term is clearly limited under the constitution, so the earlier we start, the longer we can enjoy the benefits,” Lee said, explaining why he had scheduled many overseas visits.

Seong Ghi-hong, senior presidential secretary for public relations and communication, said Lee’s remarks should be understood as ruling out any attempt to seek re-election through a constitutional amendment.

“I interpret his remarks to mean that the idea of a consecutive term — which is being discussed in some quarters — is completely impossible and not even a matter for consideration,” he told a radio programme in South Korea.
Since Cho’s remarks, the opposition People Power Party has accused Lee and his allies of considering an amendment that could allow him to remain in office.
Proposals to allow presidents to serve more than one term have repeatedly emerged since the 1987 revision of the constitution, but those attempts have failed amid political opposition.
Lee’s remarks come as his approval rating has fallen to its lowest level since he took office, with a Gallup Korea poll released last week putting it at 40 per cent. — AFP
37b9097888db8968: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The transboundary haze issue is not on the formal agenda of the 17th ASEAN Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings, but it is being discussed on the sidelines among health ministers of member states.

But as an agenda, unfortunately we are not there,” he said in a press conference after the launch of ASHA 2026-2030 here today.

e0ae4750e110ec38: KUALA LUMPUR: Pemuda Umno bersedia menyambut seruan Pemuda PAS untuk mengadakan Himpunan Mega Penyatuan Ummah, namun mahu perhimpunan itu disertai diskusi dan cadangan penyelesaian bagi masalah rakyat.

Ketuanya, Dr Akmal Saleh, berkata himpunan berkenaan tidak seharusnya sekadar menghimpunkan penyokong, sebaliknya menjadi platform untuk kedua-dua pihak membincangkan isu orang muda dan masalah negara.
“Saya sengaja tak jawab (seruan Pemuda PAS) ketika Muktamar kerana saya nak jawab pada persidangan Pemuda Umno hari ni.

"InsyaAllah jawapan kami, kami bersedia menyambut seruan itu untuk kita gerakkan (himpunan mega) satu Malaysia ini,” kata Akmal dalam ucapan dasarnya pada perhimpunan sayap itu di Pusat Dagangan Dunia (WTC).
Akmal menambah, setiap himpunan yang dianjurkan perlu mempunyai hala tuju dan menghasilkan solusi yang boleh dilaksanakan.
Pendekatan itu, katanya, selari dengan Rimbun 1.0 yang dianjurkan Pemuda Umno, termasuk perbincangan mengenai isu pendidikan.

Beliau memberi contoh beberapa cadangan yang dikemukakan melalui program itu yang kemudiannya diterjemahkan kepada dasar kerajaan, seperti penubuhan kelas Tabika Autisme Kemas yang kini telah mempunyai 19 cawangan di seluruh negara.
Akmal berkata, pendekatan sama perlu dibawa dalam Himpunan Mega Penyatuan Ummah supaya usaha penyatuan tidak terhenti pada slogan, sebaliknya menghasilkan tindakan.
“Sebab itu hari ni, bila kita nak sambut Himpunan Mega Penyatuan Ummah daripada Pemuda PAS, kita nak ada tambah baik sekali. Kita buat himpunan dan juga diskusi bersama.
“Bukan sekadar himpunan (macam) nak bebaskan Anwar Ibrahim dulu. Tetapi himpunan kita ini, himpunan yang penuh dengan solusi untuk menjawab segala permasalahan rakyat,” katanya.

Sementara itu, Akmal memaklumkan Pemuda Umno mahu menubuhkan satu pasukan khas di bawah Biro Peguam Agama sayap itu bagi membantu wanita-wanita yang 'digantung tidak bertali', apabila suami mereka gagal menjalankan tanggungjawab terhadap keluarga.
Akmal berkata, pasukan itu perlu diwujudkan bagi memastikan wanita yang berdepan konflik rumah tanggal tidak dibiarkan tanpa pembelaan kerana tidak tahu prosedur mahkamah.
“Ada suami yang dah kahwin dua. Ada suami yang dah duduk luar negara tetapi isteri masih lagi digantung tidak bertali dan perlu menanggung anak-anak.
“Anak-anak nak makan, anak-anak nak sekolah tetapi isteri ini yang menanggung. Akhirnya, ada yang digantung tidak bertali bertahun lamanya,” katanya.
Akmal berkata, pasukan khas itu akan membantu wanita terbabit memahami proses undang-undang, selain menghubungkan mereka dengan bentuk bantuan yang tersedia.
Tambahnya, Pemuda Umno turut mahu menangani isu bapa yang gagal membayar nafkah anak walaupun sudah diperintahkan mahkamah untuk berbuat demikian.
Beliau menegaskan kerajaan perlu mempertimbangkan pelaksanaan semula mekanisme potongan gaji bagi memastikan nafkah anak terbayar.
c6811688f84f5b3a: KUALA LUMPUR: Former armed forces chief Tan Sri Mohd Nizam Jaffar will stand trial for 15 days next year over four charges, including criminal breach of trust involving RM3 million.
His lawyer, Abdul Aziz Hamzah, said the trial dates had been fixed for July 26 to 29; Aug 9 to 12; Sept 13 to 15; and Sept 27 to 30.
The trial will be heard before Sessions Court judge Rosli Ahmad.
Meanwhile, Aziz said his client had instructed him to submit a representation to the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC).
A representation is usually submitted to seek the withdrawal, reduction or amendment of charges against an accused.
"Today, the defence received the complete set of documents from the prosecution.
"After perusing all the documents, I received instructions from my client to submit a representation to the A-GC.
"It will be sent within a week and we will return to court on Oct 28 for case management to update on the status of the representation.
"Meanwhile, we already have the trial dates fixed and my client is ready to go on trial. We will see how it goes and take it from there," he said.
Aziz, however, declined to disclose the nature of the representation.
On his client's health, Aziz said Nizam was facing several medical issues, including persistent knee problems, but was generally in good condition.
Deputy public prosecutor Nidzuwan Abd Latip appeared for the prosecution.
On Jan 23, Nizam pleaded not guilty to two counts of abusing his position for gratification, one count of criminal breach of trust and one count of accepting valuable items without consideration.

On the first and second charges, Nizam, who was then assistant chief of staff (personnel services) and Armed Forces Welfare Fund (TKAT) executive committee chairman, is accused of using his position for gratification totalling RM552,481.90.
The offences were allegedly committed on June 24, 2024, at the Defence Ministry, where he allegedly appointed several companies linked to his interests to supply Hari Raya gift items to TKAT.
The contracts involved the supply of pelikat and batik cloth, bath towels, backpacks and multifunctional folding pliers, with a combined value of more than RM3.5 million.

Both charges were framed under Section 23(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act, which carries a jail term of up to 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the value of the gratification or RM10,000, whichever is higher.

On the third charge, Nizam, in his capacity as assistant chief of staff and chairman of the TKAT investment committee, is accused of committing criminal breach of trust involving RM3 million belonging to the fund.

The offence was allegedly committed on Oct 4, 2024, when he allegedly dishonestly misappropriated the funds by making an additional investment in Precious Amber International Bhd without approval from the committee.
The charge was framed under Section 409 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum 20 years' jail term, whipping and a fine.
On the fourth charge, Nizam is accused of accepting RM200,000 without consideration from Aspen Red Sdn Bhd director Wan Shafie Abdul Rashid in March last year.
Nizam, who was then the armed forces chief, allegedly accepted the money with knowledge that the individual had dealings connected to his official duties at Wisma Transit Kuala Lumpur.
The offence falls under Section 165 of the same Act, which carries a jail term of up to two years, a fine, or both.
Nizam was granted RM180,000 bail with one surety and was ordered to surrender his passport to the court.

24a19dfd47924268: OSLO: Ukraine and Moldova on Wednesday played down claims from Norway's prime minister that a plane carrying President Volodymyr Zelenskyy was almost hit by a drone as it flew to Oslo.
Jonas Gahr Store told Norwegian public broadcaster NRK that Zelensky's plane was "almost hit by a drone when it was taking off from Moldova."
But a source in the Ukrainian presidency described the claim that Zelenskyy was at risk as "exaggerated."
"It was an alert in Moldova when a Russian (drone) entered Moldovan and Romanian airspace," the source told AFP.

In Chisinau, government spokesman Dumitru Ciorici said Moldova closed its airspace on Tuesday afternoon just after 4.30 pm local time due to a Russian drone that entered from the direction of Ukraine.
"The airspace was closed to protect aircraft flying over Moldova at the time: three departures and four arrivals were delayed as a result," he added.
"After 1720, the authorities confirmed that the drone had come down and exploded... some 160 kilometres (100 miles) from Chisinau International Airport.
"Flight restrictions were then lifted. For the same reason, the plane of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy took off... later than scheduled."

Zelenskyy arrived in Oslo on Tuesday evening and held talks with Store, Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg and Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide on Norwegian military aid, including air-defence support, and civilian assistance.
On Wednesday, he joined a host of other foreign dignitaries at the funeral of Norway's King Harald, who died on Aug 28 aged 89.
Zelenskyy left Norway afterwards, headed for Canada and talks with leaders there, Store told NRK.
7832d768ac4196ae: PETALING JAYA: Persidangan Komuniti Muslim Baharu (NMCC) 2026, yang akan diadakan Ahad ini bertujuan memupuk dialog berteraskan nilai kasih sayang dan rasa hormat dalam Islam, bukannya berdasarkan kemarahan, dendam atau keinginan membuktikan sesebuah komuniti itu lebih betul daripada yang lain.

Persidangan dianjurkan oleh Yayasan Al Khadeem (AKF) itu meneroka sama ada Muslim baharu, atau mualaf, mampu menjadi sebahagian jalan penyelesaian kepada wacana kaum dan identiti di Malaysia yang saban kali tegang.

Presiden dan Pengasas AKF Sheikh Hussain Yee, percaya mereka mampu berbuat demikian bukan kerana komuniti Muslim baharu ini terlepas daripada perbezaan sesama sendiri, tetapi kerana kebanyakan mualaf pernah merasai pengalaman hidup di kedua belah jurang sosial Malaysia.
"Ramai mualaf terus tinggal bersama keluarga dan komuniti bukan Muslim, sambil mengemudi identiti mereka sebagai seorang Muslim.

"Mereka merupakan golongan yang paling layak membicarakan mengenai perpecahan di Malaysia kerana mereka mengalaminya lebih daripada satu sudut pandang dalam wacana itu. Mereka memahami jurang yang wujud dan mampu membantu merapatkannya," katanya dalam kenyataan.

Selain itu, inisiatif berkenaan turut mengiktiraf golongan Muslim baharu itu sendiri tidak bersuara dari satu sudut pandang sahaja. Seperti komuniti lain, wujud pelbagai perspektif berbeza, termasuk sudut pandang ekstrem mahupun yang memilih pendekatan sederhana.
Sheikh Hussain berkata, berbanding mengelak daripada perbezaan tersebut, AKF mahu membawa semua pihak ke meja rundingan dengan cara bermartabat dan penuh hormat.

"Tujuannya bukanlah untuk mualaf mengikut sahaja kehendak masyarakat awam, mahupun bersikap mempertahankan diri secara melampau terhadap pegangan agama mereka, sebaliknya untuk mempunyai keyakinan menjelaskan mengapa mereka melihat sesuatu perkara dari sudut berbeza, sekali gus mengetengahkan pengalaman mereka bagi perpaduan negara," katanya.

Sheikh Hussain berkata, Malaysia perlu mengadakan perbincangan sedemikian, di mana ia mestilah ditangani dengan sifat kasih sayang, hormat-menghormati serta semangat kemasyarakatan yang dikongsi bersama.
Ia cukup penting terutamanya ketika wacana awam berkaitan kaum dan agama semakin tegang, dengan media sosial kerap kali memburukkan lagi salah faham dan prasangka, katanya.

"Inilah pemikiran di sebalik penganjuran NMCC kali kedua, bertemakan 'Bridging Two Worlds, Healing One Nation' yang menghimpunkan Muslim baharu, Muslim sejak lahir, dan rakyat Malaysia daripada pelbagai kaum serta latar belakang untuk sesi perbincangan mengenai pegangan agama, identiti, dan keharmonian sosial," kata Sheikh Hussain.

Barisan ahli panel terkemuka bagi persidangan tersebut merangkumi Pengerusi Eksekutif FMT Media Sdn Bhd Nelson Fernandez; pencipta kandungan dan bekas pembaca berita, Sheahnee Iman Lee; serta Pengarah Urusan MBG Fruits Adnan Lee.
Persidangan terbabit bakal berlangsung bermula 8.30 pagi hingga 6.00 petang di Grand Hyatt Kuala Lumpur.
