688693b92a935ec9: KUALA LUMPUR: Layang Layang Aerospace has voluntarily grounded its BO-105 helicopters and other aircraft equipped with Rolls-Royce 250 engines following the crash near the Long Lellang STOLport in Sarawak.

Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) CEO Norazman Mahmud said the grounding was a precautionary safety measure initiated by the operator, not an indication that the crash was caused by an engine or technical defect.
He said that, according to available records, the BO-105 helicopter's certificate of airworthiness is valid until Aug 4, 2027, while its certificate of registration is valid until July 28, 2029.

Addressing public concerns over the age of the aircraft, Norazman said age alone was not a determining factor in aviation safety, provided that the aircraft in question was properly maintained and met airworthiness standards.
He said CAAM was monitoring the operator's grounding and inspection process while verifying regulatory records for the aircraft, operator and pilot.

"The independent investigation into the accident is being led by the Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) under the transport ministry," he said after the Malaysia Aviation Safety Seminar 2026 here today.
Norazman also said CAAM was providing full cooperation and all relevant documentation.
He cautioned against speculation over whether the incident stemmed from technical faults, weather conditions or human error, emphasising that any conclusive findings must come from the AAIB.
15591e5557532a23: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno Youth is ready to work with PAS in the coming Melaka state election and believes its support among young voters can help deliver another electoral victory, Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh said today.

Akmal, who is also the Merlimau assemblyman, described Melaka as a crucial test of whether “penyatuan ummah” — the idea of uniting Malay-Muslim political parties — could be translated from political rhetoric into an actual electoral strategy.
“Melaka isn’t just a state, it’s a test — to see if we can change the reality, and penyatuan becomes a basis and not just an idea.

“Johor has decided and Negri Sembilan has decided. So I ask Datuk Seri (Zahid), Melaka should be blue as well,” he said during his speech at the Umno Youth general assembly.He said Umno Youth was prepared to repeat the strong performance it recorded among young voters in the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections.
Akmal said the wing was prepared to cooperate with PAS in Melaka, while making clear that he was not seeking candidacy for himself.
“If we work with PAS in Melaka, Datuk Seri, I repeat, at this stage as the leader of Umno Youth I do not want to become a candidate if PH is a candidate there.

“However I believe you are smart, and I’m sure you don’t want to see the Umno Youth chief not compete. We will be there with you,” he said, referring to Umno president and BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi
Akmals’ remarks come amid continuing discussions within Umno and BN over possible cooperation for the Melaka election.

He said their pursuit of Malay-Muslim political unity predated the recent Johor and Negri Sembilan elections, where cooperation between Umno and PAS had already produced results.
494c0692c7c64e0c: WASHINGTON: The US justice department (DOJ) is investigating whether Nvidia structured its licensing deal with AI chip startup Groq to avoid antitrust scrutiny, the New York Times reported on Wednesday, citing two people familiar with the matter.
Nvidia announced a US$17 billion deal with Groq last year for a "non-exclusive license" to the startup's chip technology and hired several of its executives, including founder Jonathan Ross.
The justice department opened its investigation into the arrangement shortly after it was announced in December and has sent Nvidia a formal request for information, according to the NYT report.

994bf2c4a313684b: SINGAPORE, Sept 10 — Singapore’s Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) will appeal against the reduced charge and sentence imposed on a man who assaulted a private-hire driver, saying the punishment was “manifestly inadequate”.

CNA reported that AGC filed two notices of appeal to the High Court after British citizen and Singapore permanent resident Oruche Morgan Fidelis, 23, was sentenced to a five-day short detention order and 100 hours of community service.

Fidelis had initially faced a charge of voluntarily causing hurt resulting in grievous hurt, but District Judge John Ng amended it to assault following the trial and convicted him on the lesser charge.
The 66-year-old Grab driver, Low Ek Yong, suffered a fractured skull and brain injury after the incident, although it could not be established how exactly the injuries were sustained.
Fidelis had consumed alcohol before booking a Grab ride on June 12, 2024, and became angry and pushed Low when the driver tried to wake him after they arrived at the destination.
Low died about a year later from heart disease and large bowel obstruction.
A conviction for voluntarily causing hurt resulting in grievous hurt carries a maximum jail term of five years, a fine of up to S$10,000 (RM32,200), or both.
Assault carries a maximum jail term of three months, a fine of up to S$1,500, or both.
AGC said the sentence imposed on Fidelis was “manifestly inadequate” and that its appeals would be heard by the High Court at a later date.
Fidelis was represented by lawyers from Withers KhattarWong, led by Shashi Nathan.
Offenders given a short detention order do not receive a criminal record after completing their sentence.
cf2c8a7e215e9d1c: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno will cooperate with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) if there is strong evidence to warrant prosecution against its leaders, said Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

f84cbde44b0de652: KUALA LUMPUR: Versatile actress Nabila Huda has expressed immense pride over the Indonesian adaptation of the hit 2016 Malaysian supernatural horror film, 'Munafik'.

For the 41-year-old screen star, seeing a local cinematic triumph repurposed for neighboUring markets serves as definitive proof that Malaysian storytelling possesses the artistic gravitas and universal appeal required to command the regional entertainment stage.

Nabila, whose chilling portrayal of Maria in the original Syamsul Yusof-directed masterpiece earned her widespread critical acclaim and the Best Actress trophy at the 28th Malaysia Film Festival (FFM28), believes that cross-border adaptations breathe fresh vitality into well-crafted narratives.

"When I first got wind that 'Munafik' was being remade for the Indonesian audience, my heart swelled with immense pride. It goes to show that our local cinematic output isn't merely standard fare; it carries substantial weight, distinct character, and the intrinsic muscle to command attention far beyond our shores," she said.
The original film, produced by Skop Productions, shattered local box-office records upon its release in 2016, becoming a cultural benchmark for faith-based horror thrillers in Southeast Asia.
The Indonesian adaptation, titled 'Munafik: Melawan Iblis', stars high-profile Indonesian talents including Acha Septriasa and Arya Saloka, alongside Dimas Aditya.
Reflecting on her iconic performance, Nabila admitted that stepping into Maria's tormented shoes remains one of the most physically and emotionally gruelling chapters of her acting career.
However, seeing the narrative given a new lease on life by a fresh Indonesian cast fills her with gratification rather than territorial possessiveness.

"To see another actress take on a role that was once so deeply tied to my own identity as an artiste is deeply moving. Each performer brings their own nuance and spirit to a script. I am genuinely thrilled to watch how they interpret the terrifying psychological depth of that narrative," Nabila said.
She added that collaborative ventures and content exports between Malaysia and Indonesia should be actively cultivated to elevate the regional film ecosystem as a whole.

"We have so many phenomenal stories waiting to be told. When regional powerhouses take notice and choose to reframe our narratives through their own creative lens, it elevates the entire profile of Southeast Asian cinema on the global map," she said.

3850a5d95d7bf2fb: Climate catastrophe is on our doorstep – yet Labour’s impending approval of further drilling will bring more pain for negligible gains Pinch yourself, it’s happening again. 90f9a988016375a3: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has upheld a RM920,508 award against a Penang condominium developer over missing fire doors and a wet riser room, as well as recurring defects in the common property of a luxury condominium in George Town.

Justice Alwi Abdul Wahab, who read out the unanimous judgment of a three-member bench, said there was no appealable error in the High Court judge's findings, which were firmly supported by contemporaneous documents and witness testimony.
The bench, which also comprised Justices Shahnaz Sulaiman and Amarjeet Singh, dismissed Melariang Sdn Bhd’s appeal against the High Court decision.

The dispute arose from a suit brought by the joint management body (JMB) of The Cantonment, which has since been replaced by a management corporation, over defects and omissions involving the common property of the 71-unit condominium in Jalan Cantonment.

The complaints included the omission of 101 fire doors and a wet riser room in the common areas, which were shown in approved building plans annexed to the statutory sale and purchase agreements signed by purchasers under the Housing Development (Control and Licensing) Act 1966.
The JMB also sued over the developer’s failure to satisfactorily rectify various defects, including leakage at the swimming pool and water ponding at the multi-storey car park.
Other defects included a missing water tank and pump, defective swimming pool decking, rusted grills and electrical wiring faults.

Alwi said the High Court was correct in finding that the JMB had the legal standing under Sections 143(2) and 143(3) of the Strata Management Act 2013 to sue the developer on behalf of the purchasers in relation to the common property.
He said the evidence supported the finding that the fire doors and wet riser were removed at the developer’s own request or behest.
Melariang had claimed that the items were removed following mandatory directions from the authorities.
However, Alwi said the developer failed to produce documentary evidence showing that any such mandatory direction was issued.
The appellate court also affirmed the High Court’s finding that the defects affecting the common property were recurring and had not been satisfactorily rectified by the developer.
The High Court awarded the management body RM920,508 in damages, together with RM40,000 in costs and interest at 5% per annum from the date of judgment.
The Court of Appeal ordered the judgment sum, currently held by stakeholders, to be released to the management corporation or its solicitors.
It further ordered Melariang to pay another RM50,000 in costs for the appeal.
Karin Lim and Nicholas Lim acted for the management corporation while Amrit Pal Singh and Ho You Wei appeared for Melariang.

cb4e240aa07360e8: JOHOR BARU: Johor Road Transport Department officers took action against 120 vehicles for various offences, including expired road tax, lack of insurance and driving licences, during an operation on Monday.

9b2a77ca6a5825c0: KUALA LUMPUR: Steel price continues to increase in August from a year ago, with Perak seeing the highest jump in the building material unit price index, at 6.9 per cent, followed by Johor at 6.4 per cent.

However, on a month-on-month (MoM) basis, the unit price index for steel decreased in August, ranging from -0.3 per cent to -2.4 per cent across selected areas, according to the Statistics Department.

Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan saw 2.4 per cent lower steel unit price index during the month compared with a year ago, followed by Perak (-1.3 per cent) and Pahang (-0.7 per cent).

DOSM also reported that the average price per unit of steel, consisting of mild steel round bars and Mycon 60 high tensile deformed bars, recorded a slight decrease (-0.3%) with an average price of RM3,484.20 per metric tonne as compared with RM3,496.10 per MT in July.

Besides steel, the Statistics Department also stated that the unit price index for sand increased in August, with Kota Kinabalu seeing the higher jump at 7.7 per cent, compared with in July. Perak saw 2.4 per cent jump in sand's unit price index, while the unit price index was rather flat in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan and Sibu.

Meanwhile, the unit price index for cement increased in August, but at a rather muted range of between 0.3 per cent and 0.9 per cent MoM. Kota Kinabalu again chalked the higher cement unit price index growth at 0.9 per cent, followed by Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan at 0.4 per cent.

Terengganu and Kelantan saw 0.3 per cent increase MoM on cement's unit price index. Besides that, the unit price index of this material remained unchanged in most other areas across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
However, on a YoY basis, cement's unit price index jumped 6.7 per cent in Kuching, 6.6 per cent in Miri, and 5.9 per cent in Kelantan and Terengganu
In addition, the average price of Ordinary Portland cement rose 0.3 per cent, with an average price of RM25.80 per 50 kg bag as compared to RM25.70 per 50 kg bag in July.
a752b001ca80f057: Microsoft has found another use for AI: providing an off-ramp for Salesforce customers. The software giant on Wednesday gave the world “Dynamics 365 Activate,” software that executive veep for Apps and Agents Jeff Teper described as “a comprehensive, AI-powered tool that can help partners and customers move to Dynamics 365 faster, with less manual effort and lower migration risk.” Microsoft has made the tool available as a public preview that can convert Salesforce implementations to its own SaaS-y Dynamics 365 offering. The company promises it will launch “additional CRM and ERP migration scenarios” starting “later this year.” The software behemoth’s vision for this tool is to create “one agentic implementation experience” that covers starting a new business or business process, migration from an existing tool like Salesforce, or to grow a business that already runs Dynamics. Microsoft’s explanation for how AI can move a major business application says its AI-powered convert-o-tronic machine can profile “data and entities, identify relationships and dependencies, and surface customizations that require attention.” That process apparently “gives implementation teams a clearer blueprint for what should move, what should change, and what should be redesigned before migration begins.” For Salesforce, the tool “will analyze an existing … CRM environment and build a detailed understanding of its data, business processes, customizations, and dependencies.” Microsoft’s partners are a big target for the AI-powered converter, because Redmond thinks it will help them to more quickly understand users’ existing applications. “Partners can use these insights to assess Salesforce environments faster, determine what to preserve, simplify, or redesign around AI and agents, and identify migration risks and dependencies earlier. This approach empowers teams to focus more time on solution architecture, industry expertise, and change management,” states an announcement for partners. Microsoft got serious about building a big business applications business with its 2001 acquisition of Great Plains Software. It’s hard to quantify its success because Microsoft doesn’t report a revenue line item for CRM and ERP, but the Productivity and Business Processes business unit that includes Dynamics won $140 billion of revenue in FY 26, up almost 15 percent year-over-year. It’s thought that Microsoft has earned about 25 percent market share for ERP, but just four or five percent of the CRM market which Salesforce dominates with around 20 percent share. But Salesforce customers may be ripe for a chat with an alternative supplier, as its Agentforce platform hasn’t excited users according to two recent reports – but AI spending at the CRM giant has dented its margins. Oh, the irony, that Microsoft might use AI to prise away Salesforce customers who aren’t happy with its AI! ®
fbac6293f5994c6d: PETALING JAYA: The Tapah High Court today ordered Perak executive councillor A Sivanesan to pay costs of RM3,000 to a former Penang assemblyman after allowing the latter’s application to transfer a defamation suit to a lower court.

3c16296c9728faee: SEOUL: South Korea's president has ruled out even considering to extend his constitutionally-capped one term in office, a spokesman said Thursday, after the leader and some allies had floated a reform.

President Lee Jae Myung's critics noted a second term would extend the suspension of five criminal trials against him, including on bribery charges linked to a firm's alleged illicit transfer of US$8 million to North Korea.

South Korea adopted its current single five-year presidential term in 1987 as the country transitioned from decades of authoritarian rule, in part to prevent the prolonged concentration of presidential power.
Lee said on social media in August that he favoured a four-year presidency allowing for more than one term, while shifting some presidential powers to parliament.

National Assembly speaker Cho Jeong-sik, formerly affiliated with Lee's Democratic Party, said in July that voters should decide whether an incumbent president could seek another term under a revised constitution.
Speaking to South Koreans in Paris on Wednesday during a state visit to France, Lee noted he has just one term.
"My term is clearly limited under the constitution, so the earlier we start, the longer we can enjoy the benefits," Lee said, explaining why he had scheduled many overseas visits.

Seong Ghi-hong, senior presidential secretary for public relations and communication, said Lee's remarks should be understood as ruling out any attempt to seek re-election through a constitutional amendment.

"I interpret his remarks to mean that the idea of a consecutive term -- which is being discussed in some quarters -- is completely impossible and not even a matter for consideration," he told a radio programme in South Korea.
Since Cho's remarks, the opposition People Power Party has accused Lee and his allies of considering an amendment that could allow him to remain in office.
Proposals to allow presidents to serve more than one term have repeatedly emerged since the 1987 revision of the constitution, but those attempts have failed amid political opposition.
Lee's remarks come as his approval rating has fallen to its lowest level since he took office, with a Gallup Korea poll released last week putting it at 40%.

As confirmed earlier through our official channels, in mid-June of this year, we unexpectedly received notice from PlayStation Studios that they would cancel the PHYSINT project. 253ce5fd7cb2f9c7: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — More completed homes and serviced apartments were left unsold in the first half of 2026 compared with the preceding six months, according to the Property Market Report for the First Half of 2026.

The report, released by the Valuation and Property Services Department (JPPH) today, showed that the number of unsold completed homes rose by 8.6 per cent, from 30,471 units in the second half of 2025 to 33,094 units in the first half of 2026.
Their combined value increased slightly from RM17.73 billion to RM17.78 billion.

Despite the rise in unsold properties, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the overall property market remained resilient, recording 187,320 transactions worth RM105.12 billion between January and June 2026.
Residential properties accounted for 59.3 per cent of all transactions, with 110,998 deals recorded, and contributed 44.8 per cent of the total transaction value, or RM47.11 billion.
“Although there were some marginal adjustments, the property market remain steady due to stable price movements and transaction activities as well as active construction activities.

“The stability is also influenced by the country’s monetary policy that maintained the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent, injecting confidence to both financiers and buyers,” he said before launching the report at the National Valuation Institute (Inspen) in Kajang, Selangor, today.
High-rise properties made up the largest portion of the unsold homes at 43.4 per cent, followed by terraced houses at 34.9 per cent.
About 37.3 per cent were priced at RM300,000 and below, while 38 per cent had been launched between six and 10 years ago.

Serviced apartments, which are classified separately under commercial properties, recorded a sharper increase of 24.7 per cent, from 18,752 unsold units worth RM15.42 billion in the second half of 2025 to 23,375 units worth RM19.33 billion in the first half of 2026.
More than half of the unsold serviced apartments, or 55.2 per cent, were priced between RM500,001 and RM1 million, while 71.1 per cent had been launched between six and 10 years ago.
Johor had the most unsold completed homes and serviced apartments, with 4,222 and 9,946 units, respectively.
At the same time, Johor recorded 6,697 new residential launches, the second-highest number after Selangor’s 8,354 units, while Penang ranked third with 2,878 units.
Homes priced between RM500,001 and RM1 million formed the largest segment of new launches nationwide, accounting for 10,853 units, or 39 per cent of the total.
b8503011b963d63c: SINGAPORE, Sept 10 — A commander of an Iran-backed Iraqi militia who allegedly plotted attacks against Jewish targets in Europe, Canada and the United States tried to enter Singapore on multiple occasions, the city-state’s security agency said Thursday.

Singapore said it would not have allowed Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood Al-Saadi to enter the country, but warned the case highlighted how conflicts in the Middle East could raise terrorism risks in South-east Asia.
In an annual terrorism threat assessment report, the Internal Security Department (ISD) said that Al-Saadi, who is in US custody awaiting trial, applied for visas to visit Singapore in 2023 and 2024.
“Baqer had applied for visas to visit Singapore on three separate occasions in 2023 and 2024, but did not eventually travel to Singapore,” the agency said.
The ISD said it believed Al-Saadi had travelled elsewhere in Southeast Asia during that period.
“Had he attempted to enter Singapore, he would have been denied entry,” it added.

“We do not discount the possibility that Baqer’s travel to this region could have been for terrorism purposes, and he could have set his sights on targeting Singapore, including US and Israeli/Jewish interests here.”
The agency said it was working with intelligence partners to investigate his activities.
The ISD cited the case as an example of how overseas conflicts “have heightened the threat of attack against Singapore” and South-east Asia.
Singapore and the region “continue to feel the ripple effects of the geopolitical tensions and instability in the Middle East,” it said.

Activities by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and its network of armed proxies “have elevated the threat of terrorism beyond the immediate theatre of conflict in the Middle East,” it added.
US prosecutors identified Al-Saadi in charges filed in May as a senior figure in Kataeb Hezbollah, an Iraqi armed group designated by Washington as a terrorist organisation linked to the IRGC.
According to US authorities, he directed and encouraged attacks on US and Israeli interests, and urged the killing of Americans and Jews in retaliation for the war against Iran.
He was arrested in Turkey before being transferred to the United States, where he remains in custody awaiting trial.
Kataeb Hezbollah has denied that Al-Saadi is a member of the group.
South-east Asia has been a target of militant attacks in the past, including the 2002 nightclub bombings in the Indonesian resort island of Bali that killed 202 people. — AFP
0d325d5f54668899: SYDNEY: Australia relaxed a proposed rule on Thursday that would have forced energy exporters to reserve a fixed 20% of natural gas, instead requiring them to reserve up to a fifth of production as determined by the country's energy regulator.

Energy minister Chris Bowen said exporters could provide up to 200 additional petajoules of gas per year, more than enough to avoid the possible shortfalls of up to 140 petajoules forecast by the country's energy market operator.
The proposed policy will ensure "gas is more affordable and the domestic market is always modestly oversupplied," Bowen said in a statement.
The proposal is designed to reserve an oversupply of 110% for the east coast gas market, which has faced shortfalls for almost a decade.

"The scheme ensures domestic customers can buy from a larger pool of gas, reducing the risk of tight market conditions driving price spikes, promoting long-term contracting and shielding them from global volatility," Bowen said.

"The 20% figure is a ceiling and how much an exporter must reserve for the domestic market would be determined by the Australian Energy Regulator," he said. The AER has oversight over Australia's electricity and gas markets.

The scheme's start date would also be pushed back by six months to align with the gas industry's contract cycles, meaning LNG exporters would not need to begin to meet their supply commitments until Jan 1, 2028.
Reservation levels to differ by region
The changes come four months after the centre-left Labor government proposed a hard 20% gas reservation scheme for the country's east coast market in May.

The new plan also recognises a domestic reservation requirement of 15% in Western Australia and largely exempts the Northern Territory, where holding back 20% of gas supply would vastly outweigh the region's modest demand.
Western Australia's gas supply is not connected to the east coast and the Northern Territory has one modest capacity pipeline to the east.

"Domestic supply obligations will align with physical domestic markets," resources minister Madeleine King said of the difference between western and eastern markets, noting that within an already well-supplied market, the domestic obligations would be reduced.

Three liquefied natural gas (LNG) export projects on the east coast operated by Origin Energy, Shell and Santos would be most affected by the reservation scheme, though existing contracts would be exempt.
Shares in Santos, which operates the Gladstone LNG project in Queensland, and Origin Energy, which leads rival export consortium Australia Pacific LNG, were slightly higher in early morning trade.
Australia is one of the world's largest LNG exporters and ships more gas overseas than it consumes domestically.

The government on Thursday released a draft of the policy, seeking feedback until Sept 24, after receiving more than 140 submissions from gas producers and exporters, retailers, large industrial users and trade partners during the policy's preliminary planning phase.
Australian Energy Producers welcomed the changes but warned that oversupply would flood local markets, drive down prices and discourage development of much-needed new gas supply.
"A domestic reservation policy that results in less competition and less investment is not in the national interest," a statement from the producers group said.
The bill is expected to be introduced to parliament later this year.

9fed19dfb46b37cb: PETALING JAYA: The New Muslims Community Conference (NMCC) 2026, to be held on Sunday, seeks to foster dialogue grounded in Islam’s values of compassion and respect rather than anger, resentment or a desire to prove one community right over another.

The conference, organised by the Al Khadeem Foundation (AKF), will explore whether new Muslims, or reverts to Islam, can be part of the solution to Malaysia’s often fraught conversations about race and identity.

AKF president and founder Sheikh Hussain Yee believes they can, not because the new Muslim community is without its own differences, but because many reverts have experienced more than one side of Malaysia’s social divide.
"Many reverts may continue to live within non-Muslim families and communities while navigating their identity as Muslims.

"They are the people best placed to talk about Malaysia’s divisions as they have experienced more than one side of that conversation. They understand the divides that exist and can help bridge them," he said in a statement.

But the initiative also recognises that new Muslims themselves are not a single voice. As in any community, there are different perspectives, including those at the extremes and those seeking a middle ground.
Sheikh Hussain said rather than avoiding those differences, AKF wants to bring people to the table in a dignified and respectful way.

"The aim is not for reverts to pander to wider society, nor to become defensive about their faith, but to have the confidence to explain why they see things differently and allow their experiences to bring unity to the nation," he said.
Sheikh Hussain said Malaysia needs to have these difficult conversations, which must be approached with compassion, mutual respect and a shared sense of community.
This is particularly important at a time when public discourse on race and religion is increasingly strained, with social media often amplifying misunderstanding and suspicion, he said.

"This is the thinking behind the second NMCC, themed 'Bridging Two Worlds, Healing One Nation', bringing together new Muslims, born Muslims and Malaysians of different races and backgrounds for discussions on faith, identity and social harmony," Sheikh Hussain said.

Prominent panellists for the conference include Nelson Fernandez, executive chairman of FMT Media Sdn Bhd; Sheahnee Iman Lee, content creator and former news anchor; and Adnan Lee, managing director of MBG Fruits.
The conference will be held from 8.30am to 6pm at Grand Hyatt Kuala Lumpur.
39ac3e4f955cc73c: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi today said that challenging or dismissing the royal power to grant pardons directly undermined the Federal Constitution.

During her keynote address at the Puteri Umno General Assembly, held in conjunction with the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, Amal described the royal institution as a key pillar of national sovereignty.

“Article 42 of the Federal Constitution grants the power of pardon to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, State Rulers, and Governors — challenging or dismissing this power directly undermines the Constitution itself.
“Respecting the Royal Institution and upholding the Constitution transcends partisan politics.
“Governments and political tides change, but the authority of the Monarchy and the Constitution must remain protected,” Amal said.
She added that political differences or interests were not a licence to erode the authority of the royal institution.

Also present were Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
The assembly was also attended by delegates from Singapore, Japan and the United Kingdom, as well as representatives of Ameerah Malaysia, PAS’ young women’s wing.

56abca9d0e15b48e: PETALING JAYA: Umno must not let its core principles be the first thing sacrificed when entering into any form of political cooperation, says Wanita Umno chief Noraini Ahmad.
Delivering her policy speech at the wing's general assembly today, Noraini set out five red lines for the party in any coalition arrangement.

"First: don't sacrifice the foundation of our struggle. Second: don't sacrifice the party's dignity. Third: don't sacrifice national stability. Fourth: don't sideline Malaysia's plural society. Fifth: never sacrifice the voice of the grassroots," she said.
Noraini said Umno could work with any party but warned that cooperation must not come at the expense of the party's identity.
"We can be friends with anyone. But we must know who we are," she said.
Noraini said working within a coalition of parties with differing histories and ideologies should not mean that Umno loses its voice in government.
"Cooperation must not erode identity. Identity, in turn, must not become an excuse to reject cooperation. We must be smart in safeguarding both," she said.
She said Umno joined the unity government for the sake of national stability and the people's interests, but that the party must continue to build its own strength.
"If Umno is important enough when a government needs to be formed, Umno must also be important enough when decisions affecting the people's lives are made," she said.
She said Wanita Umno understood the meaning of compromise, but too much concession could lead people to think that the party had no position of its own.
"We can sit at the same table. But we must not let our seats and our voice keep shrinking," she said.

e4623090b4cd0952: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is targeting zero fatal accidents in commercial aviation and a 90% score for the effective implementation of International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) safety standards by 2028 under a new three-year national safety plan.

0df650826e125f61: VENICE, Sept 10 — Ambitious in its scale and style and dogged by controversy, Dau by filmmaker Ilya Khrzhanovsky revisits decades of Soviet Union totalitarianism through the eyes of one of the 20th century’s great physicists.

Premiering yesterday at the Venice Film Festival, the over three-hour film was begun two decades ago by the filmmaker, who in 2024 renounced his Russian citizenship to protest the Ukraine war and now lives in Paris.

Marked by unconventional methods — including actors and extras living permanently on a massive, full-scale reconstruction of a secret Soviet research institute and instructed to remain in character — the film recounts the life of the brilliant Lev Landau, winner of the 1962 Nobel Prize in physics.
Dau, Landau’s nickname, was one of the fathers of the Russian nuclear bomb, forced by Soviet authorities to work on its development.
Khrzhanovsky, 51, said he wanted to make a film about “this generation of people, of scientists who believe that they will change the world”.
Creative and inspired, “at the end of the day they create the most terrible weapon, which could destroy everything on earth,” he told AFP in an interview.

The impressive backdrop to the otherwise intimate portrait of the proponent of free love, which spans three decades between 1938 and 1968, is a “monumental fresco of a society shaped by violence and ideology”, according to the filmmaker.
Khrzhanovsky called himself a “child of the Soviet Union”.
“And I try to understand what is it, what is this kind of Soviet thing in the DNA? Why are we like that?” he asked, speaking in English.
“What’s happened with us?”

Khrzhanovsky’s latest film is part of a larger multidisciplinary project and social experiment that includes two other films that premiered in 2020 at the Berlin International Film Festival, amid accusations of abuse and harassment during the largely improvised projects with raw, ultra-realistic scenes.
Dau took three years of filming in Kharkiv, Ukraine, between 2008 and 2011.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

(From left) Radmila Shchogolieva, Director Ilya Khrzhanovsky and Maria Nafpliotou attend the red carpet event for the screening of ‘Dau’ presented in competition at the 83rd International Venice Film Festival, at Venice Lido September 9, 2026. — AFP pic
Enemy of the state
Dau itself garnered controversy ahead of Venice after Ukraine’s government accused it of being linked to “the Russian state and its influence networks” — something the filmmaker denies.
“I’m actually the only film director for fiction movies on the list of enemies of the state,” said the filmmaker, who said he has no plans to return to his country in the near future.
“I don’t see any bright future (for Russia) for at least the next 10 years,” he told AFP.

Khrzhanovsky acknowledged taking financing for the larger multidisciplinary project from Russian billionaire Sergei Adoniev but said it was before the businessman was targeted by US sanctions over the Ukraine war.
The Ukrainian government has also criticised the filmmaker for shooting the city of Kharkiv as a Soviet city — even as it is today under bombardment by Russian forces.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Director Ilya Khrzhanovsky attends the photocall of ‘Dau’ presented in competition at the 83rd International Venice Film Festival, at Venice Lido September 9, 2026. c
Criminals and neo-Nazis

Driven by a desire to unlock the mysteries of the universe, in love with freedom and poetry, the film’s protagonist gradually sees his ideal shattered by the brutality and constant surveillance of the Soviet machine.
The film painstakingly reconstructs the famine-ravaged streets of Kharkiv in the 1930s, as well as Stalinist trials targeting recalcitrant scientists.
In one trial scene, Khrzhanovsky filmed from beginning to end without a script, with actors and non-actors invited to improvise.
“The people in the court, the judges and the prosecutor, are actually criminals, ex-criminals. People who went through many courts and they know how it, what was the protocol,” Khrzhanovsky told AFP.

“In Soviet times, judges and KGB people were actually ex-criminals. I wanted to use this kind of energy of people who have this tough nature and who are meeting intelligent and cultured people,” he said.
The director also hired real neo-Nazis for the film’s final scenes.
At a press conference yesterday ahead of the film’s premiere, Khrzhanovsky said he said he knew that “art cannot change the world”.
“But maybe it can sometimes give some feelings and emotions and more energy for some people to survive spiritually, emotionally.
“In good days, in the dark days.” — AFP

d9750b0137f35e8c: TEHRAN, Sept 10 — Oil prices hovered above US$100 (RM407) a barrel on Thursday, a day after Iran said it attacked more than a dozen vessels trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

Tehran tightened its grip on the vital oil and gas shipping route on Wednesday, expanding a no-go zone outside the waterway where it has restricted traffic since the war with the United States began on February 28.
The price of Brent crude, the benchmark international contract, was US$101.28 per barrel in early Asian trade on Thursday, after spiking above US$100 the day before for the first time since July.

The jump in crude prices came after Iranian state media reported that Tehran’s Revolutionary Guards attacked two US vessels, eight oil tankers and 10 “non-compliant vessels” trying to pass through the strait, which normally carries around a fifth of the world’s oil.

British maritime monitor UKMTO said “several merchant vessels in the Northern Arabian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman” — which surround the strait — were “subject to disabling fire as part of ongoing military activity in the region”.

President Donald Trump pledged that oil prices would come down “as soon as” the United States wins the war, which has hit an impasse more than six months after US-Israeli strikes on Tehran triggered the conflict.
“Oil will be going down as soon as we win the war with Iran,” Trump told Republicans in Texas, as the party struggles in polls against the Democrats.
“We’re winning it. We control the Hormuz Strait,” he said, repeating his suggestion of renaming the waterway as “Trump Strait”.

Trump’s optimism came despite Iran’s powerful Revolutionary Guards added parts of the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea to a new “prohibited zone” on Wednesday, saying exact coordinates will be announced later.
“If a vessel enters that area without coordination, it will be subject to our sanctions,” Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebi told state television.
Iran has asserted control of the Hormuz strait since the war broke out in February, with traffic through the waterway virtually paralysed.
Tehran requires vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the strait.
Trump said Wednesday the war would conclude right after the mid-term elections in November because Iran “can’t hold out any longer”.
However, the Wall Street Journal quoted US officials saying that Trump’s top advisers are privately warning that the war could drag on through the remaining two years of his term.
The Guards, the ideological arm of the military, also said they struck a US military base in Jordan in response to US forces destroying five Iranian oil tankers a day earlier.
Jordan’s army shot down 18 missiles fired at the kingdom, it said.

Iran’s foreign ministry condemned the attack on its oil tankers as “an overt threat to regional and international peace and security”, saying the strikes “increase the dangers of tensions in the region”.
It said the targeting of US military facilities in the region was “self-defence”.
The US military for its part had said it was responding to an Iranian attack targeting an American warship, the second such incident in less than a week.
Long war?
Iran’s Guards said the war could be brought to an end if Washington met its conditions, which included demands on the wars in Lebanon and Yemen.

“It must… refrain from renewed threats, withdraw the Israeli regime’s army from Lebanon, end the blockade of Yemen, release US$24 billion in Iran’s frozen assets and refrain from any interference in the country’s nuclear and missile capabilities,” Mohebi said, according to Fars news agency.

As Washington tries to choke off Iran economically, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) board of governors on Wednesday voted to refer Iran to the UN Security Council over its nuclear “non-compliance”, in a diplomatic move that piles pressure on Tehran.
The resolution seen by AFP was adopted by a 23-3 vote with eight abstentions, they said. Russia, China and Niger voted against it.
Iran’s representative to the UN nuclear watchdog said the resolution was passed under US pressure, saying it “has no basis and will not bring any results”.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu repeated his claim Iran was about to collapse.

“The main task is to bring down the terror regime in Iran. We are very close to that,” he said Wednesday on a troop visit in southern Syria, where Israel has occupied what it calls a “security zone”. — AFP
1f62a5fa8293cbba: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 10 — Malaysia’s draft Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Bill has been completed and will be submitted to the Cabinet, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said today.
He said the government was now setting up the structure needed to enforce the proposed law.

“We are hoping to table it this quarter or in the first quarter of next year,” he told reporters after launching the Scars of War photography and art exhibition at the Lin Xiang Xiong Art Gallery here.
The development marks the Bill’s progression beyond the drafting and public consultation stages reported earlier this year.
Gobind said the government must establish the agencies and administrative structure needed to monitor compliance and enforce the law before it takes effect.
“When we enforce a law, we must ensure there are parties that can make certain the law is complied with,” he said.
“If it is not complied with, action must be taken. That particular structure has to be set up,” he explained.

“We are looking at how to establish a structure to ensure that once the Bill is passed, there will already be parties responsible for ensuring compliance, investigating problems and enforcing the law,” he said.
Gobind said the proposed legislation would form part of a broader AI governance framework combining technical standards, regulations and laws.
“When we look at the AI governance process, it is broader than a Bill. It involves three things — standards, regulations and laws,” he said.
He said standards could address matters involving technology developers and users, while regulations would cover issues requiring closer oversight but not specific legislation.
“There are aspects that require more attention but do not reach the stage where a law is needed. In those circumstances, we look at regulations,” he said.
Gobind said regulations would allow the government to respond more quickly as AI technology evolved and new challenges emerged.
“This will be more effective because we are looking at a world where issues will arise quickly due to the nature of the technology,” he said.
He said matters requiring specific legal provisions would be addressed through the Bill, which must be tabled in Parliament.

Gobind added that AI Malaysia had been established as part of preparations for the wider governance framework, while a standards centre set up last month had begun working with SIRIM and other organisations.

8e7f40a2500fe641: KUCHING, Sept 10 — The dream of nurse Jessie Paya Jok, 44, to further her studies was cut short when she was killed in the flying doctor service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday.

0c3a8b6141a4c38a: SEPTEMBER 10 — Asean is not at war all across the region, invariably, between member states.
This has been the case since 1979. There are border conflicts but no wars between main capitals.
Yet Southeast Asia cannot assume that the absence of war means the absence of insecurity.
Indeed, the string of disasters and emergencies across maritime Southeast Asia in recent days should serve as a warning.
A fiery maritime incident near Palawan, volcanic eruptions at Anak Krakatau, forest and peatland fires, and the return of transboundary haze all point towards the delicate nature of the region.
None constitutes a war. None involves invading armies. None requires missiles or fighter aircraft.
Yet each can kill, disrupt transportation, damage livelihoods, affect public health and spill across national borders. This is the paradox Asean must understand.
Southeast Asia has been remarkably successful in preventing major wars among its member states. Analysts in Norway and Sweden refer it as “East Asian Peace.”
But the region remains exposed to another category of insecurity: natural disasters, environmental degradation, industrial and transportation accidents, extreme weather and geological instability.
The latest maritime incident near Palawan, reported by global media, illustrates one dimension of the problem.
The Philippines, like Indonesia, is an archipelagic country.
Ferries and other vessels are not peripheral forms of transportation.
They are indispensable arteries connecting islands, communities, tourism centres and local economies.
When a vessel catches fire at sea, therefore, the consequences are not merely a matter for the shipping company concerned.
They raise wider questions about maritime safety, emergency communications and the capacity of different agencies to coordinate search-and-rescue operations quickly.

Apparently ferry fires are rather common in the Philippines. Asean is, after all, overwhelmingly maritime. Indonesia and the Philippines are two of the largest archipelagic EXclusive Economic Zones (EEZs) in the world. Both are earthquakes prone.

From the Strait of Malacca to the South China Sea, from the Sulu and Celebes Seas to the waters surrounding Indonesia and the Philippines, millions of Southeast Asians depend upon maritime transportation every day.
A maritime accident in the Philippines again is therefore another reminder that human security in Asean begins with the safety of ordinary people.
Then there is Anak Krakatau. Here, some perspective is necessary.
The recent eruptions have become less intense compared with the extraordinary continuous eruptive episode earlier in September.
Indonesian geological authorities reported that the sustained eruption had ended and that subsequent activity had generally returned to shorter and more intermittent eruptions.
This is reassuring.
There is no reason to exaggerate the present situation or suggest that Southeast Asia is confronting an imminent repetition of the catastrophic Krakatau eruption of 1883.
Yet Anak Krakatau remains active and under close observation. The easing of its eruptions does not eliminate the larger lesson.
A volcano does not have to produce a catastrophic eruption before it can disrupt a modern economy.
Volcanic ash can interfere with aviation. Exclusion zones can affect maritime movements. Tourism can suffer. Transportation networks can be disrupted.
Communities surrounding the Sunda Strait can become anxious long before an eruption approaches the magnitude of a historical catastrophe.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Anak Krakatau, even as its eruptions become less intense, reminds the region about geological vulnerability. — AFP pic
Indeed, Anak Krakatau is important precisely because it demonstrates the vulnerability of modern Southeast Asia.
The more interconnected Asean becomes, the easier it is for a geographically localised disaster to produce consequences beyond its immediate location.
Then comes the haze.
This is perhaps the most familiar Asean environmental problem of all.
Forest and peatland fires can begin within national borders, but smoke recognises none of them.
The “Carbon Bombs” unleased by the forest fires in Indonesia are invariably devastating to all----as valiant efforts are made to douse them out in Kalimantan.
Winds can carry particulate pollution across Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei and, depending on atmospheric conditions, towards parts of the Philippines.
Thus, a fire in Kalimantan or Sumatra can become a health concern hundreds or even thousands of kilometres away.
Schools may be affected. Flights can be disrupted. Outdoor economic activities can decline. Hospitals can experience increases in respiratory cases.
Tourism can suffer precisely when governments are attempting to strengthen regional travel.
The haze consequently demonstrates one of the central realities of Asean: ecological interdependence is just as real as economic interdependence.
Asean cannot integrate its economies while imagining that environmental problems will remain confined behind national borders.
The same applies to floods, earthquakes, typhoons, volcanic eruptions, droughts and tsunamis.
Southeast Asia sits within one of the most geologically and climatically active regions on Earth. Indonesia and the Philippines lie along the Pacific Ring of Fire.
The region straddles major tectonic systems. Its densely populated coastlines face the consequences of rising seas and extreme weather.
Typhoons regularly strike Vietnam too.
Flooding affects Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and other member states.
Drought can undermine agriculture across the Mekong region.
Earthquakes can devastate communities without warning.
The danger is therefore not any single disaster.
It is the string of disasters.
One event may be manageable. Two occurring simultaneously place greater pressure on governments.

Several different emergencies occurring across the region can begin stretching civil-defence agencies, hospitals, aviation systems, maritime authorities and humanitarian organisations at the same time.
This is where Asean must begin thinking differently about security.

For decades, Southeast Asian security has understandably been discussed through the language of war and geopolitics: the South China Sea, US-China rivalry, Myanmar, military modernisation and competing strategic alignments.
These remain important.
But there is another security map underneath the geopolitical one.
It is a map of volcanoes, fault lines, typhoon corridors, peatlands, rivers, coastlines and heavily travelled seas.
Asean needs both maps.
The region’s great achievement since 1967 has been the avoidance of major interstate war among its members. This should never be underestimated.
In a world again experiencing wars in Eastern Europe and West Asia, Southeast Asia’s relative peace is an enormous strategic asset.
Yet peace alone cannot protect Asean from man made or natural disaster.
Asean therefore needs deeper practical cooperation on disaster preparedness and resilience.
Real-time information on earthquakes, volcanic activity, forest fires, extreme weather and maritime emergencies should move rapidly between member states.
Maritime search-and-rescue coordination must improve.
Emergency supplies should be positioned strategically. Satellite monitoring of fires, storms and volcanic ash should be shared quickly.
Civil-defence agencies should be able to communicate across borders without unnecessary bureaucratic delays.
Joint disaster-response exercises should become as routine as military exercises.
Whether it is by Five Powers Defense Agreement (FPDA) or Asean Defense Ministers Plus Arrangements (ADDMs).
This does not mean Asean should become alarmist. Quite the contrary.
The decreasing intensity of Anak Krakatau demonstrates why sober assessment is essential.
When risks decline, Asean should admit it. When risks increase, Asean must react quickly. There are more than 20 typhoons to buffet the Philippines a year, for instance.
Preparedness requires neither panic nor complacency.
What matters is recognising that the absence of war does not guarantee the absence of strategic shocks or recurring accidents.
Invariably, even the Asean Humanitarian Assistance (AHA) is in the main toothless.
Thus, a burning vessel, with hundreds missing, near Palawan can remind Asean about maritime safety.
Anak Krakatau, even as its eruptions become less intense, reminds the region about geological vulnerability.
The haze reminds Asean that environmental consequences cannot be stopped at immigration checkpoints.
Floods, earthquakes and extreme weather repeatedly demonstrate the same principle.
Asean therefore enters the final quarter of 2026 with an unusual contradiction.
There are no major wars between its member states except border skirmishes between Cambodia and Thailand in 2025.

Beliau berkata, sistem keadilan di Malaysia memperuntukkan mekanisme pelepasan secara parol dan remisi, manakala kuasa memberi pengampunan pula hak prerogatif Yang di-Pertuan Agong di bawah Perkara 42(1) Perlembagaan Persekutuan.
Justeru, kata Wee, tidak wajar bagi PH bertegas mendesak pesalah menjalani hukuman penuh tanpa mengambil kira saluran undang-undang sedia ada yang membenarkan pengurangan hukuman.

28f16a35554bb0f2: VMware has defended its decision to end public downloads of its Virtual Disk Development Kit (VDDK). VDDK is an SDK that a Broadcom technical document describes as “a set of libraries and utilities that enable software developers to create applications that can access and manipulate virtual disks used” and also “provides APIs for backup and recovery, cloning, and other operations on virtual disks.” Those qualiies mean VDDK is also useful when moving VMs from VMware to another virtualization environment. VMware’s rivals spotted that and made VDDK part of their migration tools. Nutanix’s Move, for example, requires a VDDK library to do the job. Red Hat also recommends using VDDK for migrations. ShapeBlue, an integrator that specializes in Apache CloudStack, an alternative to VMware, rates VDDK as an important part of migration tools. “The virt-v2v engine that sits underneath most VMware-to-KVM conversion work supports VDDK as an input transport,” the company wrote in late August. ShapeBlue’s post appeared a day or two after VMware, without fanfare or an explanation, took down the web pages that offered VDDK downloads. “A vendor is entitled to change how it distributes an SDK,” ShapeBlue wrote. “Doing it without a word, while the Apache CloudStack administration guide and other projects’ install instructions still tell people to click a link that no longer resolves, is something else.” “The cost lands unevenly too,” the company added. “A large backup vendor with a partner relationship has someone to call. A three-person migration consultancy, an open-source project, or a customer converting their own workloads has a forum post and a 404.” In an email to The Register, VMware defended its actions. To understand its response, know that VMware calls third party developers who work with its products technology alliance partners – aka “TAPs”. “Access to the VDDK is still available through select TAP for its licensed use case, which has always been backup and recovery,” VMware told The Register. “Customers needing backup and recovery capabilities can choose from the many approved solutions already available from these partners.” “The VDDK is not a customer entitlement. It is a software development kit covered by its own developer license and was never included with a Broadcom software purchase,” a company spokesperson added. VMware’s argument is therefore that users should not expect they can use VDDK, and that migrations is an unlicensed use case for the tool – which remains available as part of products from TAP members. VMware’s rivals have pointed out that ending public VDDK downloads could disrupt some migration projects that have already commenced, making the withdrawal of downloads jarring given the virtualization giant hasn’t previously policed use of the SDK. Services organizations that perform VMware migrations have found workarounds that make it possible to migrate VMs without needing VDDK. VMware’s decision to stop public VDDK downloads comes at a time when its changed licensing policies have seen some users either consider reducing their use of its products – as is the case at VMware channel partners like Rackspace and Macquarie Telecom – or shifting to a rival platform. VDDK has been downloadable for years and VMware cannot have been ignorant of how its rivals used the SDK to facilitate migrations. It’s therefore not hard to conclude that this is a defensive move by VMware, given it allowed downloads for years. Moving VMs is, however, among the easier parts of a virtualization migration project. Rebuilding or replacing the entirety of a virtualized environment, across networks, security, and storage, is the hard part and VMware knows it - which is why it offers a site recovery tool that doubles as a migration utility. Removing easy access to VDDK therefore doesn’t change much for those planning a move away from VMware. ®

df672ab2747406d1: From Moaz Nair
Umno’s capacity to maintain political relevance in the post-15th general election landscape demands a substantive paradigm shift.
The reconstruction of Umno’s public image must now be anchored upon three primary axes — restructuring its political narrative, systemic cleansing, and empowering dynamic human capital.
Outsourcing its political revival to PAS does not resolve Umno’s core vulnerabilities; rather, it merely masks the deeper institutional crises of corruption and patronage politics.

Umno’s political survival can no longer depend on ethnocentric hegemonic rhetoric. Instead, it necessitates a steadfast commitment to governance with integrity alongside a pragmatic adaptation to multi-ethnic political realities.
Umno cannot remain ensnared in a culture of patronage, traditional power monopolies, vulnerability to money politics, or the tendency to select candidates based on the party’s feudal hierarchy.
The contemporary political landscape demonstrates that Umno no longer monopolises the political representation of the Malay-Bumiputera community.
The emergence of new political entities grounded in alternative nationalist and religious ideologies has triggered fierce competition within the same voter market.
In this context, relying on cliché narratives such as ethnic supremacy and exclusionary sentiments towards opposing parties — specifically the DAP — is a strategy yielding diminishing returns.
Electoral data indicates that postmodern voters are more inclined to evaluate a political party based on accountability and governance efficiency.
Consequently, Umno’s future hinges on its ability to forge inclusive, cross-ethnic strategic alliances, shifting the political axis from ethnic polarisation toward policy-based competition.
To counter negative public perceptions concerning corruption and money politics, Umno requires a radical and transparent cleansing action plan.

The party’s top leadership must enforce strict disciplinary measures against members implicated in legal misconduct. Defending problematic individuals under the doctrine of absolute loyalty will only jeopardise institutional credibility.
Moving forward, Umno must position itself as a pioneer in championing the absolute independence of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission and the judiciary from any political interference.
Accordingly, vetting procedures for future electoral candidates and party positions must be tightened by prioritising integrity and technocratic capability over seniority.
Periodic mandatory asset declarations by key political officeholders (MPs and assemblymen) to an independent evaluation body are also critical to restoring public confidence.
Furthermore, Umno must advocate the establishment of a transparent political financing ecosystem to sever the chain of patronage politics that has long shackled its organisational culture.
In conclusion, restoring Umno’s image is not merely a political option but an existential necessity.

The party’s narrative must shift from mere political survival to formulating competitive and transparent public procurement policies, as external reforms remain unsustainable without preceding internal structural shifts.
The success of this transition demands strong political will from the top leadership to overhaul the organisational culture from a model of patronage politics to one of policy-driven politics.

Through concrete internal reforms and a readiness to cooperate within a pluralistic societal framework, Umno can restructure its identity as a progressive, high-integrity, and relevant party capable of navigating Malaysia’s future sociopolitical dynamics.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.

74dd8ee25e68f33d: Kita semua berasa hairan dengan sikap sesetengah pembesar adat di Negeri Sembilan, terutama dari Johol, Jelebu dan Tampin yang tidak sudah-sudah bertikai, dan sekali lagi cuba menurunkan penyandang semasa Yamtuan Besar Negeri Sembilan iaitu Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir yang memegang takhta sejak 29 Dis 2008.

Sehingga hari ini kita masih belum tahu apakah punca dan motif mereka tergamak menodai kesakralan adat tanpa segan silu. Jembalang utara, atau selatan yang manakah di belakang mereka sehingga seberani ini menderhakai Raja Berkeadilan?

Mohd Rais Yatim, pengerusi Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) yang merupakan salah satu parti komponen dalam Perikatan Nasional dan kini bekerjasama dengan Umno kelihatan tampil sebagai ‘pakar adat mereka’. Rais yang mengaku ‘pakar adat’ ini ada menukil bagaimana Adat Perpatih harus diperlakukan. Beliau menulis begini:
“When adat was the prime mover of social modus operandi in Minangkabau prior to the Pasumpahan Satie Bukik Marapalam in about 1838, the common and effective philosophy was thus:
Mamak basanda ka Pangulu Pangulu basanda ka mupakaik Mupakaik basanda ka nan bana Nan bana tagak sandirinyo

This is to say 'the mamak relies on the Pengulu who in turn relies on the rule of consensus and consensus stands on what is the truth and the truth stands on its own. It could also be argued in extension that now the system no longer relies on the truth or what is just and fair. It simply relies on the Book (the Quran) which in turn of course excretes justice and fairness. And so the shift to over-reliance on religion is the preferred mode rather than on the priority and impetus of relying on what is the truth or the just and fair disposition. The Musa Wahab case is now a milestone decision. It now settles two issues: first, the courts have no jurisdiction in adjudicating matters pertaining to the business of Undang or an adat leader succession! Second, the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang may have the prerogative of giving a blessing or otherwise in an Undangship claim. Curiously, this decision should have relied more on the force of Art. 14 of the state Constitution which states that the business of adat leadership succession should be left to the device "...in accordance with the custom of their respective luaks". The fact that more weight is given to the blessing of the Dewan has become a new yardstick hence the introduction of a new provision under Art 16(2) somewhat gives the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang a new constitutional assertion. It would appear that in future whenever the Dewan gives its blessings' the Undang candidate in a luak could mean an endorsement and this act could also mean as an interference contrary to Art. 14 of the State Constitution.”

Petikan panjang di atas terdapat dalam ‘Adat The Legacy of Minangkabau’ terbitan 2015 oleh Rais Yatim. Untuk memudahkan pembesar dan sesetengah mereka yang berdegil untuk terus berkelahi perihal kuasa ini, izinkan saya terjemahkan petikan di atas ke dalam bahasa Melayu, pandai-pandailah membacanya dalam dialek Negori:
“Apabila adat menjadi penggerak utama modus operandi sosial di Minangkabau sebelum berlakunya Pasumpahan Satie Bukik Marapalam sekitar tahun 1838, falsafah yang lazim dan berkesan adalah:
Mamak basanda ka Pangulu Pangulu basanda ka mupakaik Mupakaik basanda ka nan bana Nan bana tagak sandirinyo

Ini bermaksud bahawa mamak bersandar kepada penghulu, penghulu pula bersandar kepada keputusan muafakat, muafakat bersandarkan kepada kebenaran, dan kebenaran berdiri atas kekuatannya sendiri. Boleh juga dihujahkan bahawa kini sistem tersebut tidak lagi bersandar kepada kebenaran, atau apa yang adil dan saksama. Sebaliknya, ia semata-mata bersandar kepada Kitab, iaitu al-Quran, yang kemudiannya dianggap sebagai sumber keadilan dan kesaksamaan. Dengan demikian, berlaku suatu peralihan kepada kebergantungan yang berlebihan kepada agama, menggantikan keutamaan dan dorongan untuk berpaut kepada apa yang benar, adil dan saksama. Kes Musa Wahab kini menjadi suatu keputusan penting (milestone decision). Ia menetapkan dua perkara.
Pertama, mahkamah tidak mempunyai bidang kuasa untuk mengadili perkara yang berkaitan dengan urusan Undang atau pewarisan jawatan pemimpin adat.

Kedua, Dewan Keadilan dan Undang mempunyai prerogatif untuk memberikan perkenan atau sebaliknya terhadap tuntutan seseorang untuk menjadi Undang. Menariknya, keputusan ini sepatutnya lebih banyak bersandar pada kuasa dan maksud Perkara 14 Perlembagaan Negeri, yang menyatakan bahawa urusan pewarisan kepimpinan adat hendaklah diserahkan kepada mekanisme: “…in accordance with the custom of their respective luaks” (“…mengikut adat bagi luak masing-masing.”) Hakikat bahawa 'perkenan' Dewan diberikan lebih banyak pertimbangan telah menjadi suatu ukuran baharu. Hal ini kemudiannya dapat dilihat melalui pengenalan Perkara 16(2), yang seolah-olah memberikan kepada Dewan Keadilan dan Undang suatu kedudukan atau penegasan perlembagaan yang baharu. Nampaknya, pada masa hadapan, apabila Dewan memberikan 'perkenan' kepada calon Undang dalam sesuatu luak, perkenan tersebut boleh ditafsirkan sebagai suatu bentuk pengesahan atau sokongan.”

Baca beberapa kali biar teliti. Adalah jelas terang lagi bersuluh, bersiap huraian di atas, Rais sendiri sedar halnya. Dewan Keadilan adalah kini kuasa pengesah dalam menentukan kedudukan seseorang Undang. Ia juga tidak wajar dicabar di Mahkamah. Dan yang paling penting, Rais Yatim sendiri memutuskan bahawa setiap sesuatu itu mestilah dibuat menurut keadilan dan tentulah itu bermuarakan agama Islam.
Islam celah mana yang mereka ingin tunggang sebagai hujah? Adakah Baginda Tuanku Muhriz sudah diberi keadilan?

Dari segi adat juga, untuk menurunkan Yamtuan Besar, seorang Undang itu sendiri mesti sah di Luak masing-masing. Kita telah pun tahu duduk letak Undang di Luak Sungei Ujong, Rembau, Jelebu dalam keadaan penuh pertikaian. Malah mereka sudah dipecat oleh Waris, dan ditolak pembesar adat yang kanan di wilayah masing-masing.
Undang Sungei Ujong dan Rembau yang baru, kedua-duanya menyokong Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir. Datuk Klana Petra, Muhammad Faris Johari telah dimasyhurkan dan dizahirkan sebagai Undang.

Luak Sungai Ujong ke-11 pada Mei dan Jun 2026.Dari segi adat Mubarak Dohak telah lama ditolak. Manakala Hassan Ab Hamid telah dizahirkan sebagai Undang Luak Rembau ke-22 pada Jun 2026 berikutan adat istiadat yang sah di negeri tersebut. Beliau bersama-sama Undang Sungai Ujong telah menegaskan pendirian rasmi Luak masing-masing berkaitan hal ehwal istana dan adat di Negeri Sembilan termasuklah kedudukan Yamtuan Besar Negeri Sembilan.
Jadi celah mana yang Umno, Rais berserta segala jembalang baik utara atau selatan tidak faham?

Ternyata kerajaan Negeri Sembilan yang baru, yang turut disertai oleh Wawasan tidak mampu menyelesaikan masalah atau krisis kepimpinan adat. 6992a640d5e6c4d9: There are many things for which governments deserve criticism, and this Madani government has certainly received its fair share of reproof, sometimes deservedly and sometimes perhaps less so.

However, those of us who work in public health also have a responsibility to say clearly when the government has made the right decision in the wider public interest. This is particularly so when that decision may not be politically convenient and may expose the government to criticism from powerful interests.

The decision by health minister Dzulkefly Ahmad and the government to withdraw their appeal against the High Court judgment concerning the removal of liquid nicotine from the Poisons List is, in my view, one of those decisions.

The controversy began in March 2023, when liquid and gel nicotine for electronic cigarettes and vape products were exempted from the Poisons List before Malaysia had a comprehensive replacement regulatory framework in place. The High Court subsequently ruled that the exemption was irrational and made without proper and effective consultation with the Poisons Board, and failed to adequately protect public health and Malaysia's commitments to prevent and reduce nicotine addiction.

The government initially appealed that judgment, and many people in the public health community were disappointed because it appeared that the government intended to continue defending a decision which the court had found deeply problematic.

I also came to understand, however, why an appeal would initially be considered, because governments are institutions, and when a High Court judgment has implications for ministerial powers, taxation, existing legislation and wider administrative practice, it is not unusual for the machinery of government and the Attorney-General's Chambers to examine whether the appellate courts should consider those questions.

The government therefore exercised its legal right to appeal, but after reviewing the matter further, on Aug 18, it withdrew the appeal in its entirety and chose not to continue challenging the High Court's findings.

To me, that decision is not evidence of weakness, nor should it be presented as the government somehow surrendering to civil society, because being part of a government – in this case, the health ministry – does not mean one is compelled to defend decisions by another ministry or government arm.

Institutions and systems mature when they are able to look again at earlier decisions, consider what the courts have said, recognise when circumstances have changed, and determine whether continuing along the same path still serves the public interest. That principle is particularly important in health policy, where evidence changes, technologies change and industries adapt quickly, while the consequences of getting decisions wrong may be borne, not by institutions but by ordinary people, years later.

This is also relevant because Dzulkefly was not the health minister who made the original decision in March 2023, and his position on tobacco, vape and nicotine control has been expressed repeatedly and publicly, alongside the official direction of the health ministry.

In fact, he has made it clear that revenue collected from vape excise duties cannot in itself justify allowing harmful products to remain on sale, while making clear that future policy should be assessed according to scientific evidence, current data and public health interests – a position entirely consistent with the central lesson of the High Court judgment that economic considerations cannot displace the responsibility to protect health.

There are legitimate questions which government still needs to answer, particularly about how the Poisons Act and Act 852 now operate alongside each other, what exactly the present regulatory position is for liquid and gel nicotine, and what enforcement agencies, healthcare professionals, retailers and the public should understand the law to require.

Those operational questions are real, but they should not obscure the larger principle, because we should want governments to be capable of course correction rather than being trapped in defending yesterday's decisions simply because changing course might be politically interpreted as a loss.

We should also be realistic about what comes next, because decisions involving tobacco, nicotine and vape products do not take place in an economic vacuum, and the High Court judgment itself recorded evidence that the vape industry in Malaysia was valued at RM2.27 billion at the material time in 2023.

This is precisely why public support matters now, because if we believe the government should place public health before commercial expediency, we cannot remain silent when it actually makes a decision which moves in that direction and only reappear when there is something to criticise.

Those of us in civil society must remember the same principle, because our role is not simply to oppose the government, and our credibility depends on being prepared to recognise good decisions as clearly as we challenge bad ones.

We challenged the 2023 decision because we believed it was wrong, and we used the courts because that is one of the lawful mechanisms available in a functioning democracy. Now that the government has decided not to continue contesting the judgment, our responsibility is to acknowledge that decision fairly and work with the same government on what comes next, because disagreement does not need to become permanent hostility and, on this particular decision, the government has done the right thing.
On the nicotine appeal issue, the government did get this one right. So let’s laud them on it, and encourage further good decisions on issues affecting us, be it in health or the larger life scope.

f04c01e3426978d0: Amid industry soul-searching¹ about the possibility of AI improving itself to the point that it kills everyone, Anthropic has revealed yet another incident that would qualify as a crime if perpetrated by a person. The AI biz published "an alignment assessment" detailing four times Claude models accessed third-party systems without authorization. The company has already reported three of the incidents. Evidence of the fourth was lurking in a session transcript dating back to January 2026 when the misbehavior occurred. Anthropic found the first three by scanning around 141,000 transcripts where Claude could have obtained internet access during evaluation. It missed the fourth initially because "our scan relied on an agentic search." Felony Bench, a tongue-in-cheek record of cyber intrusions carried out by major AI companies without consequences, has added this newly-discovered incident to its rap sheet of rogue AI actions. The January 2026 AI trespass involved an early version of Claude Opus 4.6, which was given a Capture the Flag (CTF) challenge under the oversight of the third-party model evaluator where the other hacking events occurred. Opus 4.6 managed to sabotage its chances of success by disabling the machine it was targeting. It assigned the device an IP address that already existed on another piece of hardware, rendering the target unreachable and making it impossible to solve the challenge. Those familiar with other incidents where AI models violated third-party systems may recall that unsolvable tasks represent a common catalyst for misbehavior. Models exhaust all aligned options, and then turn to transgressive approaches. Opus 4.6 might have been an exception, but when it tried to abort the task after recognizing that it could not reach the target machine, it failed to do so "due to a misconfiguration in [the model's] evaluation harness." It failed to shut down not just once but seven times. So it continued onward, trying other expected means to reach the target machine but failing. Then it explored further. "The model discovered a machine belonging to a third party that it was able to access, and stated that it believed this third party was part of the CTF," Anthropic explained in its post. "Inside the machine, the model found a file listing a password, which it used to gain admin access to the system." The model went on to gather more credentials, and modified a system setting to make it easier to access the personal information of an individual associated with the third party evaluation organization. Opus 4.6 might have done more but for the fact that it exhausted its token budget, bringing the session to an end. Anthropic says it's not as concerned about this incident as the others because the model tried to abort its task. "While the model’s disregard for the possibility that it might be harming real systems or people is concerning, many of the behaviors described here have changed considerably as our training has evolved across model generations," the company said. Anthropic said it considers these incidents serious but expects current training approaches "are likely able to address the specific alignment failure modes observed in these incidents." And if company training methods fall short, there's no real consequence to anyone at Anthropic other than writing up a revised alignment assessment. ® ¹ The term "soul-searching" is figurative and is not intended to indicate a belief that the technology industry has a soul.
